(Yet) he himself is detached and untouched; the Lord is free of all ties and yet joined (with all). Whatever pleases him, he does; what the Lord does, that comes to pass. Meditate on the Lord's Name through the Guru, and the separations (from God) are lifted. ॥13॥
514.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The True One himself has (us) say Waah Waah, through the Guru's Shabad. Waah Waah is (his) praise and glory; rare is the one who understands (this) through the Guru. The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the True One; (through it) comes union with the True One. O Nanak, saying Waah Waah, God is found; (yet this praise) is obtained by his grace. ॥1॥
Waah Waah: the cry of wonder at something marvellous; in these saloks, the praise of God, for which no words are enough.
514.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The tongue that says Waah Waah is made beautiful by the Shabad. Through the perfect Shabad, God has come and been met. From the mouths of the very fortunate, (God) has Waah Waah brought forth. Those who say Waah Waah are the beautiful ones; the people come to worship them. Waah Waah is obtained by (God's) grace; O Nanak, (through it) honour is won at the True Door. ॥2॥
514.4: In the body-fortress of the proud are hard (adamantine) doors of falsehood and deceit. The blind, ignorant manmukhs, deluded by doubt, do not see (these doors). By no means are (they) found; those who wear religious garb have worn themselves out with their garbs. Through the Guru's Shabad (the doors) are opened (for those) who repeat the Lord's Name. The dear Lord is a tree of Amrit; those who have drunk (its Amrit) are satisfied. ॥14॥
514.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Saying Waah Waah, the night (of life) passes in peace. Saying Waah Waah, there is bliss for ever, O my mother. Saying Waah Waah, the attention is fixed on the Lord. Only by (God's) grace does (one) say Waah Waah, as (he himself) has it said. Saying Waah Waah, (one) wins honour. O Nanak, Waah Waah comes only by the True One's will. ॥1॥
514.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the True One; the Gurmukh has searched and found it. Through the Shabad he utters Waah Waah, and Waah Waah with his heart. Saying Waah Waah, the Gurmukh has searched with ease and found the Lord. O Nanak, very fortunate are they who keep the Lord, Har Har, cherished in their hearts. ॥2॥
514.7: O greedy mind, so very greedy, you are ever steeped in greed. Longing for enticing Maya, you roam in all ten directions. Hereafter, (your) name and caste will not go (with you); as a manmukh you suffer pain. With your tongue you have not tasted the Lord's sweet essence, and you speak insipid words. Those who have tasted the Amrit (of the Name) through the Guru are satisfied. ॥15॥
514.8: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Let us say Waah Waah to the One who is true, deep and profound; let us say Waah Waah to the One who is the giver of virtues, steady in understanding; let us say Waah Waah to the One who pervades all; let us say Waah Waah to the One who brings sustenance to all. O Nanak, knowing him as the One alone, let us praise with Waah Waah him whom the True Guru has shown (us). ॥1॥
515.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Gurmukhs ever say Waah Waah; the manmukhs eat poison and die. Waah Waah does not please them; (their life) passes in sorrow upon sorrow. Through the Guru, Amrit is (their) drink; with loving attention fixed, they say Waah Waah. O Nanak, the servants who say Waah Waah are pure; they gain understanding of the three worlds. ॥2॥
515.2: By the Lord's will the Guru is met, and one's service and devotion take shape; by the Lord's will the Lord dwells in the mind, and the essence (of the Name) is drunk in Sahaj; by the Lord's will peace is found, and the Lord's profit is earned every day; (one) is seated on the Lord's throne, and dwells for ever in one's own home (within). They alone have accepted the Lord's will who have met the Guru. ॥16॥
515.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those servants ever say Waah Waah whom (God) himself gives understanding. Saying Waah Waah, the mind becomes pure, and Haumai leaves from within. The Gursikh who says Waah Waah every day obtains the fruit the mind longs for. Beautiful are the servants who say Waah Waah; O Lord, join (me) to their company, that within my heart I may utter Waah Waah, and say Waah Waah with my mouth as well. To those who say Waah Waah, Nanak offers his body and mind. ॥1॥
515.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Waah Waah! The Master is true, whose Name is Amrit. Whoever has served (him) has obtained the fruit; I am a sacrifice to them. Waah Waah! He is the treasure of virtues; only the one to whom he gives (it) partakes of it. Waah Waah! He fills the waters and the land; through the Guru he is found. O Gursikhs, all of you, say Waah Waah every day; Waah Waah is pleasing to the Perfect Guru. O Nanak, whoever says Waah Waah in mind and heart, Jam's servant does not come near him. ॥2॥
515.5: The dear Lord is true, ever true; true is the Guru's Bani. Through the True Guru the True One is recognised, and (one's attention) merges in the True One, in Sahaj. (Such ones) keep awake night and day and never sleep; the night (of their life) goes by as they keep awake. Those who have tasted the Lord's sweet essence through the Guru's teaching are blessed beings. Without the Guru no one has found (him); the ignorant have wasted away and died. ॥17॥
515.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the Formless One; none other is as great as he. Waah Waah! He is unreachable and fathomless; Waah Waah! He alone is true. Waah Waah! He is free of all care; Waah Waah! What he does comes to pass. Waah Waah! The Name is Amrit; some rare one obtains it through the Guru. Waah Waah is obtained by (God's) grace; he himself gives (it) in his mercy. O Nanak, Waah Waah is obtained through the Guru; (the one who obtains it) takes the Name night and day. ॥1॥
516.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Without serving the True Guru, peace does not come; there is no other place (to find it). However much one may long, without (his) grace (he) cannot be found. Those within whom is the vice of greed are led astray in the love of another. Their birth and death do not end; in Haumai they suffer pain. Of those who have fixed their minds on the True Guru, not one is left empty. They are not summoned by Jam, nor do they suffer pain. O Nanak, through the Guru they are saved; they merge in the True Shabad. ॥2॥
516.2: Only the one who holds love for the Master should be called a bard; standing at (his) door he serves, and reflects through the Guru's Shabad. The bard who keeps the True One enshrined in his heart will reach (the Master's) door and home. Lofty is the bard's dwelling, through love for the Lord's Name. The bard's service and duty (is this): he repeats (the Name of) the Lord, and the Lord carries him across. ॥18॥
516.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When a Gujri, a woman of rustic caste, finds her own Husband, (it is) by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad and repeating the Lord's Name night and day. She whom the True Guru meets is filled with the fear (of God); that woman is of noble family. She alone on whom the Creator has shown grace recognises the Hukam of her Husband. That (other) one, without good ways and of ill traits, the Husband has cast off and left. When the fear (of God) takes hold, the filth (of the mind) is cut away and the body becomes pure. There is light within and the understanding becomes noble, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, the deep ocean of virtues. She sits in the fear (of God), she lives in the fear, and in the fear she does her work. Here (she has) peace and honours, and in the Lord's court the door of liberation. Through the fear, the Fearless One is found, and (her) light merges in the boundless Light. O Nanak, she who pleases the Master is the good one: she on whom the Creator himself bestows his grace. ॥1॥
Gujri: a woman of the Gujjar people, herders and sellers of milk, whose caste was counted low.
516.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Let us praise (him) for ever and ever; I am a sacrifice to the True One. O Nanak, let that tongue burn which forsakes the One and clings to another. ॥2॥
516.5: He created the partial incarnations, and he made the love of another. As kings rule their kingdoms, (so they ruled), and fought over pain and pleasure. Shiva and Brahma serve (him), yet they did not find his end. The Fearless, Formless One is beyond all sight; he is revealed through the Guru. There, sorrow and separation do not touch; (such a one) becomes steady in the world. ॥19॥
Partial incarnations (ansa avtar): in the Puranas, incarnations held to bear only a portion of the divine power.
516.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). All this, as much form as there is, is coming and going. Whoever has written this account (in the mind) has been approved. O Nanak, whoever sets himself up (as great) is a fool, an ignorant one. ॥1॥
516.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The mind is an elephant, the Guru its driver, and (the Guru's) wisdom the goad; wherever (the driver) pulls, there it goes. O Nanak, an elephant without the goad strays into the wilderness again and again. ॥2॥
516.8: My prayer is offered to him who created (all). By serving my own True Guru, I have received every fruit. I have meditated always on the Lord's Name, the Amrit; in the company of the Sants I have erased (my) pain. Nanak has become free of care, having secured the Lord's imperishable wealth. ॥20॥
517.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In the field the embankments are high, with an eye on the high house, the cloud; (so) when devotion is at home in the bride, the Friend comes (to her) as a guest. O cloud, if you are to rain, rain (now); why would you rain afterwards? Nanak is a sacrifice to those who, through the Guru, have found (the Lord) within the mind. ॥1॥
The high house is the cloud: seeing the clouds, the farmer raises the embankments of his field so that the rain-water stays in it. Mahal: wife, woman.
517.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Sweet is what pleases; a friend is one who is true and straight. O Nanak, (this) is understood through the Guru by the one in whom (God) himself makes light. ॥2॥
517.3: This is the servant's prayer before God: (O Lord,) you are the true Master. You are the protector for ever and ever; I meditate on you. Every being and creature is yours; you pervade them all. Whoever slanders your servant, you strike him down and destroy him. O Nanak, give up worry and stay free of care, clinging to (the Lord's) feet. ॥21॥
517.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Hoping and hoping, the world has died, yet hope neither dies nor departs. O Nanak, hopes are fulfilled by fixing the mind on the True One. ॥1॥
517.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Hope and desire will die (only when) he who made them takes them away. O Nanak, nothing is lasting except the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
517.6: He himself created the world, giving it a complete design. The Lord himself is the banker, himself the trader, and himself the shop. He himself is the ocean and the ship, and he himself the boatman. He himself is the Guru and himself the disciple; he himself shows the landing-place (on the far shore). O servant Nanak, meditate on the Naam, and cut away all sins.
Sudh (corrected): written after the closing numbers of the vaar, it marks that the text was checked against the original.
517.7: Raag Gujri Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). To dwell on the Guru within, and with the tongue to repeat the Guru's Name; to behold the True Guru with the eyes, and with the ears to hear the Guru's Name; steeped in (the love of) the True Guru, one finds a place in the Lord's court. Says Nanak, (God) gives this gift to the one on whom he shows grace; such ones are counted the best in the world, but they are rare, a very few. ॥1॥
517.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those whom the Protector protected, he himself has rescued; placing (them) at the Guru's feet, he has set their affairs right. He himself became merciful and did not put them out of his mind; in the company of the holy, he carried them across the world-ocean. The Saakats (those who have turned from God), the slanderers and the wicked he destroyed in an instant. In Nanak's mind is the support of that Master, remembering whom there is peace, and all sorrows go. ॥2॥
518.1: (O Lord,) you are without lineage, stainless, the all-pervading Being, unreachable and boundless. You are true, wholly true; you are seen to be true, ever true. Nothing of what you have established seems false. The Giver gives to all, as many as he has created. Stringing (all) on a single thread, he has set his light (in them). By (his) Hukam (beings are) in the world-ocean; by (his) Hukam (they) are carried across. O dear God, he alone meditates on you who has good fortune (written) on his forehead. Your state and extent cannot be perceived; I am a sacrifice to you. ॥1॥
518.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Merciful One, when you are pleased, you come to dwell in the mind, unsought; O Merciful One, when you are pleased, (we) find the nine treasures in (our own) home; O Merciful One, when you are pleased, then (we) live by the Guru's mantra; O Merciful One, when you are pleased, then, O Nanak, (we) merge in the True One. ॥1॥
518.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Many sit on (royal) seats, and sound a great many instruments; O Nanak, without the True Name the honour of none has lasted. ॥2॥
518.4: (O God,) the Vedas, along with the Kateb, stand and meditate on you; those who lie at your door are beyond all counting. The Brahmas meditate on you, and the Indras on their thrones; Shiva, Vishnu and the incarnations utter the Lord's praise with their mouths; so do the pirs, the prophets, the sheikhs, the elders and the saints (auliya). O Formless Lord, woven through all like warp and weft, you blossom in every heart. Through falsehood one works one's own ruin; through righteousness one stands firm. To whatever you yourself attach (us), to that alone we are attached. ॥2॥
The Kateb: the scriptures of the Semitic faiths (the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and the Quran).
518.5: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The heedless one) is lazy in doing good, and bold as a lion in doing evil. O Nanak, today or tomorrow the heedless one's foot will be caught in the noose (of death). ॥1॥
518.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). However many (my) wrong ways, (your) love does not stay hidden. Says Nanak: you, my Husband Lord, the true Friend within the mind, have covered (them). ॥2॥
518.7: O Merciful One, I ask this of you: make me the slave of your servants. I obtain the nine treasures and a kingdom; by uttering (your Name) I live. The treasure of the Amrit Naam is plentiful in the homes of (your) servants. In their company I am delighted, hearing (your) praise with my ears. I do their service, and (my) body is made pure. Waving the fan, (carrying) water, grinding (the corn) and washing (their) feet, I rejoice. By myself nothing can be done; O God, look on (me) with your glance of grace, and let me, who have no virtue, be given a place in the dharamsal (house of worship) of the Sants. ॥3॥
518.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Friend, may I ever remain the dust of your feet. In your refuge, may Nanak see you ever present. ॥1॥
518.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Countless fallen ones become pure when (their) mind is attached to the Lord's feet. God's Name is the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage; O Nanak, (it comes to the one) on whose forehead good fortune is (written). ॥2॥
518.10: With every breath and every morsel, let the Name of the Sustainer be repeated always. The one on whom he shows mercy, he does not forget. It is he who creates, and he himself who destroys. The Knower knows everything; understanding, he gives it thought. In an instant he sets up the creation in countless forms. The one he joins to the Truth, him he saves. The one on whose side he stands never loses. His court stands forever, never broken; I bow to him. ॥4॥
519.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Lust, anger and greed should be given up; let them be burned in the fire. O Nanak, while we live, let us repeat the True Name every day. ॥1॥
519.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering his God again and again, he has obtained all the fruits; O Nanak, the one who has worshipped the Naam has been united (with God) by the Perfect Guru. ॥2॥
519.3: He is liberated (while living) in the world, whom the Guru has instructed. His affliction is gone, (his) anxieties are erased. Beholding the sight of him, the world is delighted. In the company of (God's) servant one is delighted, the filth of sins washed away. There the True Name, the Amrit, is repeated. The mind finds contentment, and the hungry one is satisfied. The one in whose heart the Name has come to dwell has his bonds cut away. By the Guru's grace, only some rare one earns the wealth of the Lord. ॥5॥
519.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In my mind I think this thought: that I should rise each day and make the effort; O Lord, Friend of Nanak, give (me) the occupation of the Lord's Kirtan. ॥1॥
519.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those whom God has kept safe by casting his glance (of grace): their mind and body are dyed in the Primal Lord. O Nanak, (so it is with) those who are pleasing to God; I, poor one, am dying in pain. ॥2॥
519.6: Whatever pain there is in your heart, lay it before the Guru in prayer; give up all your cleverness, and offer up your mind and body (to him). Worship the Guru's feet, and evil-mindedness burns away. In the company of the holy, cross the terrible world-ocean. Serve the True Guru, the divine one; you will not die of fear in the hereafter. In an instant he brings delight, filling the empty to the brim. The mind finds contentment when the Lord is meditated on always. He alone takes up the True Guru's service on whom (God's) grace rests from the very beginning. ॥6॥
519.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (My love) is fixed in the right place; the Joiner has joined it. O Nanak, the other waves number hundreds of thousands, (but) my Beloved does not let (me) drown. ॥1॥
519.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the dreadful forest I have found one companion: the Lord's Name, the remover of pain. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the beloved Sants; (through them) Nanak's tasks are fulfilled. ॥2॥
519.9: All treasures are obtained by being dyed in your love. Repeating your (Name), there is no regret. No one can reach (the standing of) your servants, who lean on you. Praise, praise to the Perfect Guru! Remembering (him) in the mind, I find peace. The treasure of praise is with the Guru; it is obtained by (God's) grace. When the True Guru looks (on one) with his glance of grace, there is no more wandering. The Merciful One himself protects (them), making them his own servants. I live by hearing, again and again, the Name of the Lord, Har Har Har Har. ॥7॥
520.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You, my Husband Lord, have given (me) the silk robe of love to keep my honour covered. My Master is wise and all-seeing; Nanak does not know your worth. ॥1॥
520.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through remembering you I have found everything; I have seen no hardship. O Nanak, the one whose honour the True Master keeps, no one can erase (it). ॥2॥
520.3: Great peace comes when the Merciful Lord is meditated on; heaps of diseases are destroyed when the Lord's praises are sung; coolness pervades within when God comes to mind; hope is fulfilled when the Name is enshrined in the mind. No obstacle comes in the way when self-conceit is lost; the treasure of divine wisdom (comes) when understanding is received from the Guru. He alone has obtained all things to whom (God) himself has had them given. (O God,) you are the Master of all; all are in your shelter. ॥8॥
520.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As I cross the (world-) river, my foot does not sink (in the mire), for within me is love for you. O Husband Lord, I have stitched my heart to your feet; for Nanak, the Lord is the raft and the boat. ॥1॥
520.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those at whose sight evil-mindedness departs: they alone are our friends. I search the whole world; O servant Nanak, (such friends) are a rare few. ॥2॥
520.6: (O God,) seeing your devotees, the Master comes to mind; dwelling in the Saadh Sangat, the mind's filth is cut away; repeating the Shabad of (God's) servant, the fear of birth and death is cut away. The Sants untie the bonds, and all the demons run and hide. They attach (our) love to him who upholds all (creation), the unreachable, the infinite, whose seat is the highest of the high. With palms joined, day and night, he should be meditated on with every breath. When he himself becomes merciful, then the company of the devotees is found. ॥9॥
520.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the alien wilds there is stifling heat and turmoil, and cries ring out on the roads. O Husband Lord, my cord is tied to you; (so) Nanak passes through the forest in bliss. ॥1॥
520.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). True fellowship is with those in whose company the Name is repeated. O Nanak, no company should be kept with those who care (only) for their own ends. ॥2॥
520.9: Approved is that moment in which the True Guru is met. When the company of the Saadh is found, pain does not strike again. The unshakeable place is found, and one does not lie in the womb again. The One, Brahm, is seen in all. The essence of wisdom (comes) by fixing the attention (on God) and drawing the gaze in (from outward things). It is all the repetition of (God's Name), whatever is spoken by the mouth. Understanding the Hukam, one is delighted, and dwells in peace upon peace. Those whom (God) has tested and placed in (his) treasury are never counterfeit again. ॥10॥
520.10: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The pangs of separation are pincers (of torture), so harsh they cannot be borne. If that Master is met, O Nanak, then truly (there is) every comfort. ॥1॥
Jambur: pincers with which flesh was torn from the body in torture.
521.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The earth dwells in water; wood keeps fire (within it). O Nanak, (such) is that Husband Lord, on whose support everyone rests. ॥2॥
521.2: (O God,) the works you have done are within your power alone; that alone comes to pass in the world which you have ordained from the very start. We are struck with wonder and awe, seeing your creation. (We,) your servants, have fallen at your refuge; be gracious, that I may be set free. The treasure is in your hands; you give it to the one who pleases you. Those on whom (you) become merciful, they alone receive the Lord's Name. O unreachable, imperceptible, infinite (Lord), your end cannot be found. The one on whom you are gracious meditates on the Naam. ॥11॥
521.3: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The ladles move about (in the food) but do not know its taste; they stay empty. Those faces alone look (lovely), O Nanak, that are dyed in the relish of love. ॥1॥
521.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through the tracker (the Guru) I have traced the footprints (of those who) had laid (my field) waste. You, my Husband Lord, have given (it) a fence; O Nanak, the field is not laid waste (now). ॥2॥
521.5: Worship that True One, in whose keeping is everything. He himself is the Master of both ends (this world and the next), and in an instant he sets (all affairs) right. Give up all (other) devices, and take hold of his shelter; run and fall into his refuge, and gain the joy of all joys. (Good) deeds, dharam and the knowledge of the essence: (all) come with the company of the Sants; when the Amrit Naam is repeated, no obstacle stands in the way. The one to whom he himself is kind: in that one's mind he comes to dwell; when the Master is pleased, all treasures are obtained. ॥12॥
521.6: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have found the One worth finding, for my Beloved has shown grace. There is one Creator alone; O Nanak, no second is seen. ॥1॥
521.7: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Drawing the arrow of Truth, throw down the wretched sins; keep the Guru's sweet mantra in mind, O Nanak, and sorrow will not come. ॥2॥
521.8: Praise, praise to the Creator, who himself has brought cool peace. Always repeat (the Name of) him who is kind to all beings and creatures. The Mighty One has shown mercy, and the wailing and lament are over; fevers, sorrows and diseases have fled, through the glory of the perfect Guru. Honouring the lowly and setting them firm, he has given (them) his own protection; he himself has set (them) free, cutting away all bonds. Craving is quenched, hope is fulfilled, the mind is sated with contentment. The boundless Master is the greatest of the great; neither virtue nor sin leaves a stain on him. ॥13॥
521.9: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those on whom God becomes merciful, they alone repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. O Nanak, as soon as they meet the Saadh Sangat, their love is drawn to Ram. ॥1॥
521.10: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remember Ram, O fortunate ones; he is in the water, on the land and in the sky. O Nanak, when the Name is worshipped, no obstacle stands in the way. ॥2॥
521.11: What the devotees say is approved; it finds acceptance in the Lord's court. (O Lord,) your devotees lean on you; they are dyed in the True Name. The one to whom he is merciful: that one's pain departs. O Merciful One, the devotees are your own; you bestow your kindness on them. Pain, suffering, grave disease and Maya do not touch such a one. This is the devotees' support: they sing the praises of Govind; for ever and ever, day and night, meditating on the One alone, and drinking the Amrit Naam, (the Lord's) servants remain sated with the Naam. ॥14॥
522.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Millions of obstacles beset the one who forgets the Name; O Nanak, (such people) wail night and day, like a crow in a deserted house. ॥1॥
522.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When union with the Beloved comes about, that alone is the lovely season. May he not be forgotten for a moment or an instant; O Nanak, let him be remembered always. ॥2॥
522.3: (The five vices) are brave warriors and heroes, whom no one has held back; the five have gathered a mighty, stubborn army; the ten women (the organs) make even ascetics who have renounced the world cling (to pleasures); conquering (all) one by one, they take them into their own ranks: this alone is what they want. (The world of) the three qualities is in their power; no one has turned them back. Doubt is (their) fort and Maya the moat: say, by what means can it be broken? By worshipping the perfect Guru this fearsome army is smashed. Before him I would stand day and night with joined hands. ॥15॥
522.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Sing (his) praises day after day, and all sins are washed away; O Nanak, if the Name is forgotten, millions of torments spring up. ॥1॥
522.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Nanak, when the True Guru is met, the way (of life) becomes perfect; (then,) while laughing, playing, dressing and eating, liberation comes in the very midst (of it all). ॥2॥
522.6: Blessed, blessed is that True Guru, who has torn down the fort of doubt. Praise, praise to that True Guru, who has joined (us) to the Lord. The Guru gives the Naam, the treasure that never runs out, as medicine; it is he who has destroyed the great and dreadful disease. The treasure of the Naam is found, a vast store of riches; this priceless (human) birth is won, and one's own self is recognised. The greatness of the mighty Guru, the Divine One, cannot be told; the Guru is the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, beyond the farthest beyond, unseen and unfathomable. ॥16॥
522.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Making the effort, live (the true life); practising (it), enjoy peace; meditating, meet God; O Nanak, (so) anxiety is lifted. ॥1॥
522.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Good thoughts, the uttering of Gobind's praises, the pure company of the Saadh (be mine); have mercy, O Lord, that I, Nanak, may not forget the Naam for even a moment. ॥2॥
522.9: (O Lord,) if (all) that happens is your doing, why should we be afraid? The one meeting whom the Name is repeated: to that one let (our) soul be offered. When the Master beyond count comes to mind, (the heart) is filled with joy. Who can harm the one on whose side the Formless Lord stands? Everything is in his power; no one is outside (it). That (Lord) has come to dwell in the minds of the devotees; through Truth he is absorbed (in them). Your servants meditate on you; you are (their) Protector. Almighty over all, you make (them) glad with your glance of grace. ॥17॥
523.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) take away lust, anger, intoxication (of pride), greed, attachment and evil desires; keep (me) safe, O my own God; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥1॥
523.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Eating and eating, the mouth has worn out; wearing (clothes), the whole body (too); O Nanak, cursed is the life of those whose love has not been fixed on the True One. ॥2॥
523.3: As your Hukam is, just so it has to be; wherever you yourself keep (us), there (we) must go and stand. In the love of your Name, evil-mindedness is washed away; repeating you over and over, O Formless Lord, doubt and fear are cast away. Those who are dyed in your love are not yoked to births (again); within and without, their eyes behold the One. Those who have recognised the Hukam never have to weep; O Nanak, they string the Name, (God's) gift, into their minds. ॥18॥
523.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). While alive he did not remember (the Lord); dead, he mingles with the dust; O Nanak, the foolish and unclean Saakat has passed (his life) with the world. ॥1॥
523.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The one who) remembered the Lord while living, and in dying (stayed) in the Lord's love, has carried the precious gift of birth across, O Nanak, in the company of the Saadh. ॥2॥
523.6: From the beginning, from the start of the ages, (God) himself is the Protector; the Creator's Name is True, and the True One pervades (all). Nowhere is he lacking; he fills every single heart. Merciful and mighty, he himself makes (us) do the labour (of devotion). Those in whose minds he himself has come to dwell are at ease for ever. Having made the creation himself, he himself has cherished it; he himself is everything, endless and boundless. With the support of the perfect Guru, Nanak has kept (him) in remembrance. ॥19॥
523.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the beginning, in the middle and at the end, the Supreme God has protected (his servant); the True Guru has given (him) the Lord's Name, and (he) has tasted the Amrit. (His is) the boundless company of the Saadhs, and night and day he dwells on the Lord's virtues; he has gained every wish of his heart, and does not wander through births. All lies in the Creator's hands, who brings about (every) cause. Nanak begs for this gift: that by the dust (of the feet) of the Sants he may cross over. ॥1॥
523.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Enshrine in your mind the One who created (you). Whichever servant has meditated on the Master has found peace; that Gurmukh's life has borne fruit, and his coming (into the world) is accepted. Understanding the Hukam, he is in bliss: (the Hukam) the Master has decreed. The one to whom (God) himself has become merciful does not wander in doubt; whatever the Master has given, he has found it to be joy. O Nanak, the one to whom the Friend is kind, he makes (him) understand the Hukam; those whom he himself leads astray die over and over and are ever born again. ॥2॥
523.9: (God) struck down the slanderers at once, and did not let them stand for even an instant. God cannot bear (his) servant's pain: seizing (the slanderers), he has yoked them to births. By the hair of their foreheads he has dashed them down, and cast them on the road of Jam. Struck by pain, they cry out, and lie in dreadful hell. Hugging (his) servants to his breast, O Nanak, the True Lord has kept them safe. ॥20॥
524.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeat (the Name of) Ram, O fortunate ones; he fills the water and the land. O Nanak, when the Name is meditated on, no obstacle stands in the way. ॥1॥
524.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Millions of obstacles beset the one who forgets the Name; O Nanak, (such people) wail night and day, like a crow in a deserted house. ॥2॥
524.3: Remembering the Giver over and over, (my) heart's aims are fulfilled; the wish and the hope of the mind are fulfilled, and the sorrows are gone. The treasure of the Naam is found, which (I) was seeking; (my) light has merged with the Light, and the toil is over. In that house peace, Sahaj and bliss have come to dwell; coming and going have ended; there is no birth there, nor death. Master and servant are seen to be one and the same; by the Guru's grace, Nanak has merged in the True One.
524.4: Raag Gujri, the hymns of the Bhagats. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Ghar 2, a Chaupada of Sri Kabir Ji. With four feet and two horns, and a mouth that cannot speak, how then will you sing of (the Lord's) virtues? Whether you rise or sit, the stick will fall on you; where then will you hide your head? Without the Lord, you will become an ox in another's hands, with torn nostrils and broken shoulders, eating the chaff of kodo millet. Roaming the forest all day long, even then your belly will not be full. You do not heed what the devotees, the Lord's servants, tell you; you will reap what you yourself have done. Going through pain and pleasure, sunk in great delusion, you will wander through countless births. You have thrown away the jewel of (human) life and forgotten God; where will you find this chance again? Going round and round like an oil-presser's ox, the night (of your life) will pass without release. Says Kabir: without the Name of Ram, you will beat your head and regret. ॥4॥
Kapi is read, as the traditional commentators read it, as the oil-presser's ox, which circles the press all night and gets nowhere.
524.5: Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Kabir's mother weeps, sobbing again and again: O Raghurai (the Lord), how will these children live? Kabir has left off all his work, the setting of the warp and the weaving, and has written the Lord's Name upon his body. Kabir answers: as long as I am running the thread through the eye of the bobbin, so long does Ram, the Beloved, slip from my mind. My understanding is shallow, and by caste I am a weaver, (yet) the Lord's Name is the profit I have gained. Says Kabir: listen, O my mother: for us and for these (children) the Giver is the one Raghurai. ॥4॥
525.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Pade of Sri Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (O Lord,) if you give (me) a kingdom, what glory is that (to me)? If you make me beg for alms, what would I lose? O my mind, worship the Lord, (in whom is) the state of nirban; your coming and going will not happen again. (O Lord,) you created all, and you have led all astray in doubt; the one to whom you give (it), that one alone has understanding. If the True Guru is met, doubt goes. Whom shall I worship? No other comes into my sight. One stone is treated with love, (and) on another stone the foot is set. If that one is a god, then this one too is a god. Says Namdev: as for me, (I am in) the Lord's service. ॥4॥
525.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. No stain of dirt is on him; he is beyond all dirt; like a fragrance, he has come and settled (in every heart), O sister. No one saw him coming; who can know (him), O sister? Who can describe him? By whom can he be understood? The beautiful Lord (Ramaiya) fills all, O sister. As the track of a bird in the sky cannot be traced, as the path of a fish in water cannot be seen, as a pot in the sky, filled with the water of a mirage, (cannot be grasped), (such is) Bithal, the Master of Nama, who has burned away the three (fevers). ॥3॥
525.3: Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, Pade of Sri Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The calf has already made the milk its leavings, at the very udder; the flower the bumblebee has spoiled, and the water the fish. O mother, what shall I bring to offer in the worship of Gobind? I find no other flower, none beyond compare. The sandal trees of Malaya have snakes coiled round them; poison and Amrit live side by side. Incense, lamps, food offerings: their fragrance (has already been taken); how, then, are your servants to worship you? I offer up my body and mind; this is the worship I lay before (you); by the Guru's grace I attain the Pure One. Worship and adoration (with such offerings) are not mine to give you; says Ravidas: what, then, will my state be? ॥5॥
Malaya: the hills of South India famed for sandalwood, round whose trees snakes are said to coil. By tradition, poison and Amrit both came out of the ocean when it was churned.
525.4: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Pade of Sri Trilochan Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (If) the inner self, filthy (as it is), has not been made pure, (and) outwardly (one wears) the garb of a renunciate, (if) the lotus of the heart and Brahm within the body have not been recognised, why become a sannyasi? (The world) has strayed in doubt, O Jai Chand; it has not, not at all, recognised the Lord of supreme bliss. (One) ate from house to house and fattened the body, (put on) the patched coat and the earrings, (all) for Maya; (one) smeared on the ashes of the cremation ground, (but) without the Guru the essence was not found. Why do you chant, why do you practise austerities, why do you churn water? Remember the One beyond desire, who created the eighty-four lakh (forms of life). Why (carry) the water-pot, O wearer of the patched robe? Why wander to the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage)? Says Trilochan: listen, O mortal: where there is no grain, why spread (the sheaves) for threshing? ॥4॥
526.1: Raag Gujri, the hymn of Bhagat Trilochan Ji. One who at the very end thinks of wealth, and dies in such thoughts, is born again and again as a snake. O sister, may the Name of Gobind not be forgotten. One who at the very end thinks of (his) wife, and dies in such thoughts, is born again and again as a prostitute. One who at the very end thinks of (his) sons, and dies in such thoughts, is born again and again as a pig. One who at the very end thinks of mansions, and dies in such thoughts, is born again and again as a ghost. One who at the very end thinks of Narayan, and dies in such thoughts, says Tilochan: that man is liberated; Pitambar, the Lord, dwells in his heart. ॥5॥
Trilochan speaks in the terms of the belief, common in his day, that the last thought at death shapes the next birth. Pitambar (clad in yellow): a name of Krishna, which he uses for the Lord.
526.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, a Pada of Sri Jaidev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (He is) the Supreme, the Origin (of all), the all-pervading Being, beyond compare, endowed with truth and every such quality; supremely wondrous, beyond Prakriti (the stuff of the world), beyond the reach of thought, reaching everywhere. Only the Name of Ram, which delights the mind, utter: it is Amrit, the very essence; by remembering it, the fear of birth, of old age, of (the mind's) ills and of death no longer torments (one). If you wish to overcome Jam and his kind, (then) praise (the Lord): that is well-being, that is the good deed to do. In the present, the past and the future he is wholly imperishable; he is supreme, and ever in bliss. Greed and the rest, the eye cast on another's home, conduct that goes against what is right, give up all evil deeds and evil thinking, and run to the refuge of Chakradhar, the Holder of the discus. The Lord's own devotees are wholly pure, in heart, in deed and in word; what (is gained) by yoga, what by sacrifices, what by charity, what by austerities? Repeat Gobind, Gobind, O man: (he is) the abode of all spiritual powers. Jaidev has come openly to his (refuge), who in the present and the past reaches everywhere. ॥5॥

Jaidev writes in a language close to Sanskrit, and its case endings decide the sense: jasamarnen is by remembering it, and jogen, jagen, daanen and tapsaa are by yoga, by sacrifice, by charity, by austerity.

489.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) I would make your Name the sandalwood, if my mind were the stone (to grind it on);
if good conduct were mixed in as the saffron, worship would be done within the heart itself.
The worship to be done is to meditate on the Naam; without the Name no worship is done.
The images of the gods are washed outwardly; if someone washes the mind (in that way),
his impurity is removed, the soul is scoured clean, and his journey is to liberation.
Beasts win praise: they eat grass and give Amrit (milk).
Cursed is the life of men empty of the Naam, and the deeds they do.
He is near; do not think him far; he ever looks after (us) and takes care (of us).
What he gives, that (we) eat; says Nanak, he alone is the True (Master). ॥4॥
489.2: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Brahma sprang from the lotus at (Vishnu's) navel, and recites the Vedas with his mouth, his throat tuned;
(yet) the end of that (Lord) cannot be seen; (Brahma) keeps coming and going in darkness.
O Beloved, support of my breath of life, why should you slip from my mind?
(You are the One) whose devotion the perfect devotees perform, whom the sages serve through the Guru's wisdom.
The sun and the moon are his lamps; the one Light of Murari fills the three worlds.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh stays pure day and night; the manmukh is in the darkness of night.
The Siddhas go into Samadhi and are ever in strife; what can (one) see with the two eyes?
When the True Guru settles the strife, the Light within and the melody of the Shabad awaken.
O Master of gods and men, infinite, unborn, boundless One in the true mansion,
may Nanak meet (you) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), O Life of the world; cast your glance of grace and carry (him) across. ॥4॥
490.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Cursed is such a life, in which love for the Lord is not gained,
(and cursed the) work in which the Lord is forgotten and one goes and clings to another.
O mind, serve such a True Guru, by serving whom love for Govind wells up and all else is forgotten;
the mind stays held to the Lord, there is no fear of old age, and the rank of (true) life is gained.
Through love for Gobind a (rare) Sahaj has welled up; see what a (wondrous) devotion has come about!
Through the self itself, self-conceit has been eaten up; then the mind became pure, and (its) light merged in the Light.
Without good fortune such a True Guru is not found, though everyone may long (for him).
(When) the wall of falsehood within is taken away, then there is peace for ever.
O Nanak, what service can that servant render such a True Guru? He lays his very life before the Guru,
(and) keeps the True Guru's will in his mind; the True Guru himself shows (him) grace. ॥4॥
490.2: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O brother, serve the Lord; serve no other.
By serving the Lord, the fruit the mind longs for is gained; in other service, life passes in vain.
O brother, the Lord is my love and my way of life; the Lord is my talk, the Lord my story.
By the Guru's grace my mind is soaked (in the Lord's love); this is the service that befits me.
The Lord is my Simriti, the Lord my Shastra; the Lord is my kinsman, the Lord my brother.
I hunger for the Lord; with the Lord's Name my mind is filled; the Lord is my kin, who becomes my companion at the end.
Without the Lord all other wealth is false; it does not go along at the time of departure.
The Lord is my wealth; he goes along with me; wherever I go, there he goes.
False is he who clings to the false; false are the deeds he does.
Says Nanak, (this) is the Lord's will that has come to pass; nothing can be said (of it). ॥4॥
490.3: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the world the Naam is hard to obtain; it is obtained through the Guru.
Without the Name there is no liberation; let anyone weigh it and see.
To my Guru I am a sacrifice, for ever a sacrifice.
Meeting the True Guru, the Lord dwells in the mind, and one stays absorbed in Sahaj.
When (the Lord) puts his fear (in one), detachment (bairag) springs up and comes into the mind.
Through detachment the Lord is found, and one stays merged in the Lord.
They alone are liberated who conquer the mind; Maya does not come and cling to them again.
One who makes his dwelling in the Tenth Gate gains understanding of the three worlds.
Says Nanak, through the Guru (the disciple) has become the Guru; behold his will!
The Creator himself brings this about, and one's light merges in the Light. ॥4॥
491.1: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Everyone says Ram, Ram, but by (mere) saying Ram is not attained.
(When) by the Guru's grace Ram dwells in the mind, then one gains the fruit.
One in whom love for Govind takes hold within,
never forgets the Lord; (such ones) say Har Har ever in mind and heart.
Those in whose hearts deceit dwells, who outwardly have themselves called Sants,
their craving never ends at all; at the end, departing, they repent.
Though one strives at many places of pilgrimage, the Haumai within never goes.
The man whose duality does not go, Dharam Raj punishes him.
Only the one blessed with grace finds (him); through the Guru a rare one understands.
O Nanak, (when) one kills Haumai within, then that one meets the Lord. ॥4॥
491.2: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
That person has peace and an ever steady understanding, whose pride (the Lord) takes away.
That person is pure who understands through the Guru and fixes his mind on the Lord's feet.
O heedless mind, remember the Lord, and the fruit you wish for will be yours.
By the Guru's grace you will find the Lord's sweet essence; if you go on drinking it, you will be at peace for ever.
When the True Guru is met, one becomes the paaras; having become the paaras, one is revered.
Whoever reveres him gains the fruit; he gives instruction and makes (others) understand the True One.
Without (becoming) the paaras there is no reverence; (yet one) whose own mind is not won over instructs others.
The ignorant blind man calls himself a guru; whom can he set on the path?
O Nanak, without (the Lord's) glance of grace nothing is gained; one on whom he casts his glance gains (it).
By the Guru's grace (the Lord) grants glory and dispenses his Shabad. ॥4॥
491.3: Raag Gujri, Panchpade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Wisdom does not spring up (by going to) Kashi, nor is wisdom lost (by staying away from) Kashi.
Meeting the True Guru, wisdom springs up, and then one gains this understanding.
O mind, listen to the Lord's praises, and enshrine the Shabad in the mind.
(Then) this understanding of yours will hold steady, and doubt will go from within.
Enshrine the Lord's feet in your heart, and (your) sins will be destroyed.
If you bring under control the self made of the five elements (the mind), then you dwell at the place of pilgrimage.
The manmukh's mind is foolish; it gains no understanding at all.
He does not understand the Lord's Name, and in the end departs repenting.
This mind is Kashi, all the places of pilgrimage and the Simritis: the True Guru has made this understood.
The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage stay with the one in whose heart the Lord remains absorbed.
O Nanak, meeting the True Guru, the Hukam (God's will) is understood, and the One has come to dwell in the mind.
(O Lord,) all that pleases you is true; (one who knows this) stays merged in the True One. ॥5॥
492.1: Raag Gujri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O pandit, the one Name is the treasure; hear it and learn it; he alone is true.
Whatever you read in the love of another, in reading and reckoning there is ever pain.
Stay attached to the Lord's feet; through the Guru's Shabad understanding comes.
Taste the Lord's sweet essence with your tongue, and the mind becomes pure.
Meeting the True Guru, the mind is content, and then there is no more thirst or hunger.
Whoever has found the treasure of the Naam goes to no one else's house.
Though the manmukh may talk and speak, he gains no understanding.
Through the Guru's teaching there is light in the heart; that one gains the Lord's Name.
Even hearing the Shastras you do not understand, and so you wander again and again.
He is a fool who does not know his own self, and does not set his love on the True One.
The True One has led the world astray; nothing can be said (of it).
O Nanak, he does whatever pleases him, as is his will. ॥5॥
492.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O servant of the Lord, True Guru, True Being, I make my plea before you, Guru:
we are lowly worms and insects, True Guru, come to your refuge; be merciful, and make the Naam shine (in us).
O my friend, divine Guru, make the Lord's Name shine in me.
May the Naam, received through the Guru's teaching, be the companion of my life, and the Lord's praise my provision for the road.
Great, very great, is the fortune of the Lord's servants who hold faith in the Lord, Har Har, and who thirst for the Lord.
On receiving the Name of the Lord, Har Har, they are fulfilled; and in the Sangat (the company of the holy), virtues shine forth in them.
Those who have not found the Lord's sweet essence, the Naam, are unfortunate, and in the grip of Jam (the messenger of Death).
Those who have not come to the True Guru's refuge and his Sangat: cursed is their living, and cursed their hope of life.
The servants of the Lord who have found the True Guru's Sangat had this written on their foreheads by the Lord from the start.
Blessed, blessed is the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), in which the Lord's sweet essence is found; O Nanak, meeting in it, the Naam shines forth within. ॥4॥
492.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Govind, Govind, the Beloved: the Beloved (dwells) in the mind; joining the Sat Sangat, through the Shabad, he captivates the mind.
Repeat Govind; Govind is the One to meditate on; that God alone gives gifts to all.
O my brothers, Govind, Govind, Govind has captivated my mind.
I sing the praises of Govind, Govind, Govind; meeting the Guru, in the Saadh Sangat, (the Lord's) servant shines.
Devotion to the Lord is the ocean of peace; by the Guru's teaching, Kaula (Lakshmi), riddhis and siddhis come to lie at (the devotee's) feet.
The Name of Ram is the servant's support; repeating the Lord's Name, he shines in the Lord's Name.
The evil-minded are unfortunate, their understanding insipid; hearing the Naam, anger rises in their minds.
Put the essence of Amrit before a crow, and it is satisfied (only) eating filth, dung in its beak.
The True Guru, who speaks the truth, is the pool of Amrit; bathing in it, the crow turns into a swan.
O Nanak, blessed, blessed and most fortunate are those whose hearts' filth the Naam, (received) through the Guru's teaching, washes away. ॥4॥
493.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's servants are exalted; exalted is the word they speak with their mouths, for the good of others.
Whoever hears it with faith and devotion, the Lord in his grace carries him across.
O beloved Ram, unite me with the Lord's servants.
My beloved, my breath of life, is the True Guru, the Perfect Guru; the Guru has carried me, a sinner, across.
The Gurmukhs are fortunate, most fortunate, whose support is the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, the Lord's sweet essence, they obtain; through the Guru's teaching (theirs are) the storehouses of devotion.
Those who have not had the sight of the True Guru, the True Being, are unfortunate, struck down by Jam.
They fall into the wombs of dogs, swine and donkeys; struck down by God, they are great slayers.
O Merciful to the meek, be kind to your servant; in your grace, save (him).
Servant Nanak is in the Lord's refuge; if it pleases the Lord, the Lord carries (him) across. ॥4॥
493.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
(O Lord,) be merciful and attach my mind (to you), that night and day I may meditate on the Name of Ram, ever.
The Lord is all peace, all virtues, all treasures; repeating him, all pain and hunger depart.
O my mind, the Name of Ram is my friend, the Lord (my) brother.
Through the Guru's teaching I sing the praise of the Name of Ram; at the end (it is my) helper, and sets (me) free in the Lord's court.
You yourself are the Giver, God, the Knower of hearts; in your grace (you) have put a longing in my mind.
In my mind and body a longing for the Lord has taken hold; God has fulfilled the longing in the True Guru's refuge.
The human birth was gained through merit; without the Name it is cursed, cursed, and goes in vain.
Without the Name, (one) who eats the sweet and the savoury eats only pain; his mouth stays insipid, and spit upon spit is cast in his face.
To those servants who are in the refuge of the Lord God, Har Har, the Lord, Har Har, gives glory in his court.
God says to his servant: Blessed, blessed, well done! O servant Nanak, he clasps (him) to his bosom and unites (him with himself). ॥4॥
493.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O my Gurmukh friends and companions, grant me the gift of the Lord, who gives life to my breath.
May I be the servant, the slave, of the Guru's Sikhs who night and day have meditated on the Lord God, the all-pervading Being.
In my mind and body a longing for the feet of the Guru's Sikhs has taken hold.
O Sikhs of the Guru, my brothers, friends of my breath, instruct me, so that, brought (by you), the Lord may meet me.
When it pleases the Lord God, he unites (me) with the Gurmukhs, to whose minds the words of the Guru, the True Guru, are pleasing.
Most fortunate are the Guru's beloved Sikhs: (meeting) the Lord, who is free of desire, they have attained the state of nirban.
Dear to the Lord is the Guru's Sat Sangat, (the company) of those to whose minds the sweet Name of the Lord, Har Har, is pleasing.
Those who have not found the company of the True Guru's Sangat are unfortunate sinners, devoured by Jam.
God, the Merciful, himself shows mercy; the Lord himself, through the Guru, is met, brought (by him).
Servant Nanak utters the Bani of (the Lord's) virtues; through Gurbani he is merged in the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
494.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Of those who have (found) the True Guru, the Being, may one who has found the Lord God give me his teaching and make the Lord sweet to me.
Mind and body grow cool and are made wholly green in the fortunate one who meditates on the Lord's Name.
O brother, may someone come and meet me who will make the Lord's Name firm (within me).
To that beloved I would give my life, my mind, my body, everything, who would recite to me the praises of my Lord God.
Patience, dharma and the Lord are found, through the Guru's teaching, by the one who ever fixes his mind on the Lord's Name, on the Lord.
The True Guru's Bani is words of Amrit; whoever speaks it puts Amrit into his mouth.
The Name is pure, and through it no dirt clings; (whoever) repeats the Name by the Guru's teaching is lovingly absorbed (in the Lord).
Those who have not found the precious wealth of the Name are luckless and dead; (such a one) dies and is gone.
(You are) the root of bliss, the life of the world, the Giver; O Lord, you give bliss to all your servants, to each who meditates on you.
You are the Giver; all beings are yours. O servant Nanak, (the Lord) forgives and, through the Guru, unites (them with himself). ॥4॥
494.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Mother, father and son are all made by the Lord;
the Lord has made the bond among them all.
O my brother, all our strength has come to nothing;
body and mind, all is the Lord's; the body is in the Lord's power.
The Lord himself has given his devotees loving faith (in him),
and in the very midst of household life he keeps them detached.
When love for the Lord has formed within,
then all that (one) does pleases my Lord God.
To whatever task, whatever work the Lord sets us,
that we do, what he himself has us do.
Those whose devotion has pleased my God,
those people, O Nanak, are lovingly attuned to the Name of Ram. ॥5॥
495.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O mind, why do you keep brooding over your efforts (to earn), when the dear Lord is engaged in the task (of caring for you)?
He has created creatures in rocks and stones, and set their food ready for them beforehand.
O my dear Lord (Madho), those who have joined the Sat Sangat have crossed over.
By the Guru's grace they have attained the supreme state; the dry wood has turned green.
Mother, father, people, sons, wife: no one is anyone's support.
The Master delivers sustenance to each and every one; O mind, why are you afraid?
(The crane) comes flying hundreds of kos (leagues), her little ones left behind.
Who is there to feed them, to give them grain to peck? She keeps them remembered in her mind.
All the treasures and the eighteen siddhis rest in the palm of the Master's hand.
O servant Nanak, let us be a sacrifice, a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice to him; (O Lord,) your extent has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥4॥
495.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Worldly people perform rituals and the six rites, and are steeped in these;
(but) the filth of Haumai within is not washed away; without the Guru they lose the game (of their life).
Show mercy, my Master, and save (me).
Among millions, hardly one is (your) servant; all the others are traders (bargaining for their own ends).
(I) have searched the Shastras, the Vedas and the Simritis, all of them; all proclaim one thing:
without the Guru no one attains liberation; reflect on it in your mind and see.
(People) have dipped and bathed at the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage) and wandered over the whole earth;
day and night they keep many rules of ritual purity, (but) without the True Guru there is darkness.
Running and running, (we) have roamed the whole world; now (we) have come to the Lord's door.
(the Lord) has wiped out evil-mindedness and lit up the understanding; O servant Nanak, through the Guru (he) has carried (us) across. ॥4॥
495.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord's wealth is (my) chanting, the Lord's wealth (my) austerity, the Lord's wealth the food that pleases (me).
I do not let the Lord, Har Har, slip from my mind for an instant; it was in the Saadh Sangat that (I) found (this wealth).
O mother, the son has come home with his earnings:
the Lord's wealth as he walks, the Lord's wealth as he sits, the Lord's wealth waking and asleep.
The Lord's wealth is (my) bathing at the holy places, the Lord's wealth (my) wisdom; (I) fix my attention on the Lord.
The Lord's wealth is the raft, the Lord's wealth the boat; the Lord, Har Har, ferries (me) to the far shore.
The Lord's wealth has made me forget my anxiety; the Lord's wealth has taken away (my) doubt.
From the Lord's wealth I have gained the nine treasures; the Lord, the whole store, has come into my hands.
Eat it and spend it, it never runs short; it stays with (one) in this world and the next.
The Guru has loaded up the treasure and given it to Nanak; this mind is dyed in the Lord's love. ॥4॥
496.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one in whose remembrance all sins are destroyed and the ancestors too are saved,
that Lord, Har Har, repeat always, who has no end and no far shore.
O son, this is (your) mother's blessing:
may the Lord, Har Har, never slip from your mind for an instant; remember the Lord of the world always.
May the True Guru be merciful to you, and your love be for the company of the Sants;
may the Supreme God guard (your) honour like clothing, and Kirtan (the singing of his praises) be (your) food every day.
Drink the Amrit and live long, for ever; remembering the Lord, (know) endless bliss.
(May you have) joy and delight and every hope fulfilled; may anxiety never touch you.
May this mind of yours become the bumblebee, and the Lord's feet the lotus;
servant Nanak clings to them, as the chatrik (rain-bird) blossoms at the raindrop. ॥4॥
496.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One) makes plans to go west, (but the Lord) takes (him) east instead.
In an instant he can set up and pull down; the last word is in his own hand.
Cleverness is of no use at all;
whatever my Master has determined, that is what comes to pass.
In the very midst of the desire to win lands and amass wealth, the breath departs;
leaving armies, deputies and attendants, all, (he) rises and departs for the city of Jam.
(Another), with his mind's stubborn resolve, turns from all else and makes a show of himself;
what was not to be condemned he condemned and gave up, and that very thing he eats again and again.
The one to whom (the Lord), of his own nature, has been merciful: that person's noose he has cut.
Says Nanak, (one who) has met the Perfect Guru is accepted, whether householder or renunciant. ॥4॥
496.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Each one who has repeated the Naam, the treasure: their bonds have been cut away.
Lust, anger, the poison of Maya, the sense of mine: from these ailments they have turned back.
(The one who) has sung the Lord's praise, joining the Saadh Sangat:
by the Guru's grace (his) mind has become pure, and (he) has found the peace above all peace.
Whatever (God) has done, (he) accepts as good; such is the devotion (he) has practised.
Friend and foe are all alike (to him); this is the mark of the way of Yoga (union with God).
The all-pervading (Lord) fills every place; (he) has known no other anywhere.
(God dwells) within each and every body, in all, without a gap; (that servant) delights (in him) with love, dyed in his love.
When Gopal (the Lord who sustains all) became kind and merciful, (he) came into the home of the Fearless One.
In an instant strife and anguish were wiped away; O Nanak, (he) merged in Sahaj. ॥4॥
497.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whatever man I take my plea to is filled with his own sorrow.
The one who has worshipped the Supreme Lord in his heart has crossed the ocean of fear.
Apart from the Guru and the Lord, no one cuts away (the mind's) pain and sorrow.
If one forsakes God and becomes another's servant, by that, one's honour, greatness and good name decline.
The ties of Maya, friends and kin, were of no use whatever.
The Lord's servant, though of low birth, is high; in his company the fruits the mind longs for are gained.
(There may be) hundreds of thousands, millions of the delicacies of Maya: in them thirst was not quenched.
Remembering the Naam, a light as of millions shone, and the Thing beyond the reach of the senses came into view.
Wandering and wandering, (I) have come to your door, O Lord, my King, destroyer of fear.
(Your) servant longs for the dust of the feet of the Saadh (the Guru); Nanak has found this peace. ॥4॥
497.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, a Panchpada, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
First (one) dwells in the mother's womb; leaving that place, (one) comes onto the earth.
Painted halls, beautiful gardens, mansions: nothing of these goes along.
All other greed and craving is false;
the Perfect Guru has given the Lord's Name; this alone is the thing that becomes the soul.
Wrapped up in dear friends, kinsfolk, sons, brothers and wife, (one) laughs;
(but) when the final hour arrives, death seizes (him) before their very eyes.
Doing wrong upon wrong, (he) gathered riches, gold, silver and money;
the hired man got (only) his wage, and all the rest became another's.
Fine horses, fine elephants and chariots (he) collected, and took care to make them his own;
(but) once the long journey began, they do not go a single step (with him).
The Naam is wealth, the Naam the king of comforts, the Naam family and helper.
The Guru has given Nanak the riches of the Naam; it does not die, nor does it come and go. ॥5॥
497.3: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, Tipade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Sorrows are gone, peace has made its home (within), the burning of craving is quenched;
the True Guru has made the treasure of the Naam firm (in the heart); (one) neither perishes nor comes and goes.
Repeating the Lord's Name, the bonds of Maya have snapped.
My God became kind and merciful, and joining the Saadh Sangat (we) were set free.
At all hours (he) sings the Lord's virtues, drunk with the delight of devotion and love;
in joy and in grief alike (he) stands apart; (he) has recognised the Creator.
The one to whom (he) belonged has saved (him), and (his) whole way of life has come right.
Says Nanak, God, the Being, is merciful; (his) worth cannot be told. ॥3॥
498.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(God) has made the fallen pure and made them his own; all bow before them.
No one asks (their) varna or caste; (all) long for the dust of (their) feet.
O Master, such (is the power of) your Name.
(You) are called the Master of the whole creation, (yet) the side you take for your servant is beyond compare.
In the Saadh Sangat Nanak has gained (this) understanding: the Lord's Kirtan is the support.
Namdev, Trilochan, Kabir the humble servant, and the Chamar (Ravidas) have been set free. ॥2॥
498.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is no one able to understand (him); who knows what (he) is like?
Shiva, Brahma and all the silent sages cannot grasp (his) state.
The account of God is beyond reach and beyond fathoming.
(Of him) one thing is heard, and it is grasped in another way; (he) lies beyond all speaking and telling.
(He) himself is the devotee, himself the Master, absorbed in himself.
Nanak's God pervades all; (I) have seen (him) everywhere. ॥2॥
498.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Counsel, consultation, other cleverness: the servant (of God) knows none of these.
Wherever an occasion arises, there (he) meditates on the Lord.
To love devotion is God's age-old way.
(He) cherishes (his servant) like a child, and lavishes his affection on him.
In place of repetition, austerity, self-restraint, rites and dharma, the servant has sung the Lord's Kirtan.
Nanak has sought the Master's refuge, and has received the gift of fearlessness, and peace. ॥2॥
498.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Worship the Beloved day and night; do not delay even for the blink of an eye.
Serving the Sant (the Guru), let us set our faith (on the Beloved), giving up stubborn pride.
The Enchanting (Lord) is the pride of my life, ever full of joy.
He dwells close beside (my) heart; seeing his play, the mind is enchanted.
He in whose remembrance the mind finds bliss and the rust comes away from the mind:
Nanak cannot describe the glory of meeting him; it is beyond the farthest beyond. ॥2॥
498.5: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who are called munis (silent sages), yogis and knowers of the Shastras: (Maya) has brought them all under her own sway.
The three gods and the thirty-three crore (gods): there was no end to their wonder.
Mighty (Maya) holds sway over the whole earth;
no one else knows her secret; by the Guru's grace it has been found.
Conquering and conquering, she has conquered every place; she clings to all the worlds.
Says Nanak, from the Saadh (the Guru) she has fled; becoming his handmaid, she clasps his feet. ॥2॥
499.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Joining both hands, (I) made my plea and meditated on my Master;
giving his hand, the Supreme God has protected (us) and wiped out all the evil.
The Master himself has become merciful;
all is well, all has become bliss; the children of Gopal are saved.
Meeting the Husband (Lord), the brides have sung songs of joy, the Master's acclaim.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru who has saved all. ॥2॥
499.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Mother, father, brothers, sons, kinsfolk: their strength is slight.
(I) have seen Maya's many shows; not a shred of it goes along (with anyone).
O Master, without you I have no one.
I am without a protector and without virtue, with not one merit; I have longed for your support.
I am a sacrifice, again and again, to your feet; here and hereafter, your strength is (my stay).
Nanak has had the sight of you in the Saadh Sangat, and all dependence (on others) is gone. ॥2॥
499.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Sant) makes one give up household entanglements, delusion and attachment, and joins one's love to God;
he makes this teaching firm in the mind: sing (God's) praises in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj.
O friend, such a helper is the Sant (the Guru):
meeting him, the bonds of Maya break, and (God) is never forgotten.
After trying again and again in many and various ways, (I) have settled on this as best:
whoever, meeting the Saadh (the Guru), sings the Lord's praise, O Nanak, crosses the world-ocean. ॥2॥
499.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) can set up and pull down in an instant; his worth cannot be told.
In a moment he makes a king a pauper, and sets (his) light in the lowly.
Let us always meditate on our own Lord;
why worry and fret over that (world) in which (our stay) is but a moment?
O my perfect True Guru, I lean on you; (my) mind has fallen into your refuge.
Says Nanak, we are heedless, ignorant children; protect us, placing your hand (over us). ॥2॥
499.5: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are the Giver of all beings; dwell within my mind.
Where (your) lotus feet are enshrined in the heart, there is no delusion and no darkness.
O Master, the moment I remember (you), you are right there.
Show mercy, O Sustainer of all, that I may ever praise God.
May I cherish your Name with every breath; O God, it is you alone I long for.
Nanak has come to lean on the Creator; he has cast off other hopes placed in others. ॥2॥
500.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Master,) in your mercy grant me the sight of you, that I may sing your praise night and morning.
With my hair may I dust the feet of (your) servants: this is my one wish.
O Master, apart from you there is no second.
O Lord, I think of you in my heart, worship you with my tongue, and keep my eyes on you.
O merciful, all-pervading Being, Master of all, with joined hands I make this prayer:
may Nanak, your servant, keep repeating the Name; (so) he will be saved in the blink of an eye. ॥2॥
500.2: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Maya) has come rushing from the realm of Brahma, the realm of Rudra (Shiva) and the realm of Indra;
but she cannot so much as cast her eye on the Saadh Sangat; she rubs and washes (their) feet.
Now I have come and fallen into (the Guru's) refuge.
The hidden fire (of Maya) burns fiercely: this the True Guru has made known to me.
She stays wound about the necks of Siddhas, seekers, Yakshas, Kinnars and men.
(But) God the Creator has taken the side of his servant Nanak, he who has millions of such handmaids. ॥2॥
500.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Through remembrance) ill repute is wiped out, there is honour in the world, and a seat is found in the Lord's court.
The dread of Jam ends in an instant, and one goes home in peace and bliss.
(Remembrance,) through which no labour goes to waste:
remember your God at all hours; let us meditate on him always, with mind and body.
O destroyer of the pains of the poor, I am in your refuge; what you give, O God, that alone we receive.
O Nanak, (the Lord's servants) are dyed in love for (his) lotus feet; the Lord keeps the honour of his servants. ॥2॥
500.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Sustainer of the world is the Giver of all beings; (his) storehouses are full of devotion.
Service to him never goes without fruit; he saves (his servant) in an instant.
O my mind, be absorbed in (his) lotus feet;
ask of him alone, whom all beings worship.
O Creator, Nanak is in your refuge; you, O God, are the support of (my) life.
Whom you protect, becoming his helper, what can the world do to him? ॥2॥
500.5: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Lord) himself has upheld the honour of his servant.
The Guru gave the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as medicine, and all the fever has gone.
In his mercy the Supreme God has saved Hargobind.
The illness is gone and every comfort has come, through ever dwelling on the Lord's virtues.
My Creator has taken (me) as his own; this is the greatness of the Perfect Guru.
The Guru has laid an unshakeable foundation, O Nanak, which rises higher day by day. ॥2॥
500.6: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(I) never set my mind on the Lord;
my life has passed in worldly affairs, and (I) did not sing the Name of the treasure of virtues.
Scraping together penny by penny with deceit, (I) ran about, using many schemes.
How many of the sorrows that come from forgetting God can be counted? The great enchantress (Maya) has devoured (me).
Be kind, my Lord; do not count what I have done.
O Gobind, merciful, compassionate, ocean of peace, O Lord, Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥2॥
501.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With your tongue keep uttering Ram, Ram;
leaving other, false dealings, worship the Lord God always.
The one Name is the devotees' support, their stay here and hereafter.
In his mercy Gobind has given (them) the Guru's wisdom and a discerning intellect.
(They) have grasped the refuge of him who is the Cause of creation, the all-powerful, Sridhar.
The dust of the Saadh's feet is the way to liberation; O Nanak, (they) have found the treasure of the Lord. ॥2॥
501.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Give up all your cleverness and come into the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru);
sing the praises of God, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God.
you will find every comfort and well-being, and all trouble will end.
Mother, father, son, friend, brother: apart from him, none is (your own).
Here and hereafter he is the soul's companion, he who pervades all.
Millions of efforts and devices are false; none of them is of any use.
In the Saadh's refuge one becomes pure, and through God's Name comes liberation.
God is beyond reach, merciful and lofty; he is able to give refuge to the holy.
O Nanak, he is found by the one for whom union was written from the very start. ॥4॥
501.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Serving your own Guru, dwell ever on the virtues of Gobind;
with every breath worship the Lord, Har Har, and the mind's anxiety will lift.
O my mind, repeat God's Name;
you will find peace, Sahaj and bliss, and you will gain a pure abode.
In the Saadh Sangat save this mind, and worship (God) at all hours;
lust, anger and pride will be destroyed, and all trouble will end.
The Lord is unshakeable, indestructible and unfathomable; come into his refuge.
In your heart worship (his) lotus feet; fix your attention on the One.
Those on whom the Supreme Lord God showed mercy, he himself forgave,
and gave (them) the Lord's Name, which (brings) every comfort; O Nanak, repeat (the Name of) that God. ॥4॥
501.4: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Whoever) by the Guru's grace meditated on God, (his) doubt was shattered;
sorrows, darkness and fears were destroyed, and (his) sins ran out.
(One) whose mind holds love for the Name of the Lord, Har Har,
(and who,) meeting the Saadh (the Guru), meditates on Gobind through his word: most pure is (his) way of life.
Recitations, austerities and countless deeds find their fruit in remembering the Name.
Those whom (God) in his kindness has himself protected: (their) works are fulfilled.
May I never forget you at any breath, O Brahm, all-powerful God.
(His) virtues are many; what can the tongue tell of them? They are countless, ever beyond words.
Taking away the pain of the poor, (God) carries them across; he is merciful, the bestower of grace.
Remembering the Name, the everlasting state (is reached); O Nanak, hold firm to the refuge of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
502.1: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
An ego-bound intellect and the dense (hold of) Maya: this is a great, lingering disease.
The Lord's Name is the medicine; the Guru has given the Name of him who is the all-able Cause of creation.
With mind and body let us long for the dust (of the feet) of the Lord's servants;
(through it) the sins of millions of births are washed away; O Gobind, fulfil (this) longing.
At the beginning, at the end and in between, hope is a fearsome she-dog.
Through the Guru's wisdom and singing the Kirtan of Gobind, the net of Jam is cut.
Those plundered by lust, anger, greed and attachment ever come and go (in birth and death).
Through love for God, devotion to Gopal and remembrance, the wandering through births is ended.
Friend, son, wife, dear well-wisher: the three fevers burn them all.
Repeating Ram, Ram, he ends his sorrows who meets the Lord's servants, the Sants.
Wandering every way, (people) cry out, but nowhere is there release.
Nanak has firmly grasped the refuge of the feet of the Lord, infinite God, (his) shelter. ॥5॥
502.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
