Worship Sridhar (the Lord), whose very form brings fulfilment, the all-able Cause of creation.
Uttering (his) praises and hearing (his) boundless glory, one is never parted (from him) again.
Through remembrance, strife and sorrow pass away; (so) cut the noose of Death's messengers.
Uttering the Lord's Name burns up the enemies (within); there is no other remedy.
Be kind, O my God; the Name is Nanak's (life's) purpose. ॥2॥
502.3: Raag Gujri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are all-powerful, the giver of refuge, the destroyer of sorrow, the king of peace.
Singing your pure praises, O God, troubles go, and fears and doubts are wiped away.
O Govind, without you there is no other place (for me).
Have mercy, O Supreme Lord, my Master, that I may repeat your Name.
Those who, serving the True Guru, cling to the Lord's feet have, by great good fortune, their attention fixed (on him).
In the Saadh Sangat the lotuses (of their hearts) have opened, and they have given up a corrupt intellect.
One who sings the Lord's praises at all hours and remembers (him), merciful to the meek,
crosses over himself; all his company is saved as well, and all his entanglements are destroyed.
O God, my Master, your feet are (my) support; God is with (me), through and through, like warp and weft.
Nanak has come to your refuge, O God; the Lord has given (him) his hand and kept him safe. ॥4॥
503.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In the one city (of the body) five thieves dwell; though held back, (each) runs off to steal.
Whoever guards his wealth from the three (qualities of Maya) and the ten (senses), O Nanak, attains release and liberation.
Keep in mind Vasudev, Banwali (the Lord);
let the Lord (dwelling) in the heart be (your) rosary.
That (tree) whose root is above and whose branches are below, to which the four Vedas are attached,
falls away with ease from those, O Nanak, who stay awake, their attention fixed on the Supreme Lord.
In the courtyard of my house (my heart) is the Paarjat (the Lord), the Essence (of all), (the world its) flowers, leaves and branches;
(he is) the Light in all, the Pure One, Sambhu (the self-existent): give up your many entanglements.
Listen, you who seek instruction: Nanak prays, give up the net of Maya.
(One whose) attention, through reflection in the mind, is fixed on the One has neither birth nor death again.
That one alone is called Guru, Sikh and physician who understands the (patient's) sickness.
Because of that (remembrance), no work or business (binds him); not (caught) in the world's business, though a householder, he is a yogi.
He has cast off lust, anger and pride, greed, attachment and the thirst for Maya;
in his mind he has meditated on the Essence, the Unmanifest, and by the Guru's grace has found (him).
Knowledge (of God) and meditation are all spoken of as (his) gift; (before the one who has it) all the fiends (the vices) turn pale.
He savours the honey of the lotus that is God; he stays awake and does not sleep.
(That tree, the Lord,) is deep beyond measure, its leaves reach down to the netherworlds; O Nanak, it pervades all.
By my Guru's teaching, no more shall I come into the womb; making me leave the poison, he has given me Amrit to drink. ॥8॥
503.2: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O God, the Giver, who are all those who beg of you? There is no end to their number.
Whatever the hunger deep within (a person), you, the True One, are able to give (to meet it), O Giver.
O dear Lord, you, the True One, are (my) chanting, austerity, self-discipline and support.
Give (me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (through which) peace is found; the stores of devotion to you are full.
(Then) you remained in the trance of Sunn, absorbed (in yourself); you alone, the One, reflected on your own Hukam.
There was then no water, land, earth or sky; O Creator, you yourself made yourself manifest.
Then there was no Maya, none absorbed (in it), no shadow (of it); no sun or moon, nor any other light.
The eye that sees all was within (you yourself); that single glance (of yours) keeps watch over the three worlds.
He made air, water and fire, and the forms of Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh.
All are beggars; you, God, are the Giver, who gives gifts as he himself sees fit.
The thirty-three crore (gods) beg of you, O God, the Leader (of all); for all your giving, your stores never run short.
Nothing goes into a vessel turned upside down; into an upright one Amrit falls, by (his) gracious glance.
The Siddhas, in their trance, beg (of you); begging for riddhis and siddhis, they hail your victory.
Whatever the thirst within the mind, water of that kind you give.
Those of great fortune serve their Guru; there is no difference between the Gurdev and Murari.
Neither death nor Jam casts an eye on those who, within, grasp the Shabad through reflection.
Now and ever I ask nothing else of the Lord: O Pure One, lovingly give (me) the Naam.
Nanak, the chatrik, begs for the Amrit-water: O Lord, in your mercy grant (him) your praise. ॥8॥
504.1: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O dear one, (a person) is born and dies, comes and goes again; without the Guru there is no liberation at all.
Mortals steeped in the Naam through the Guru have found liberation and honour through the Naam itself.
O brother, set your mind on the Lord's Name;
by the Guru's grace, beg (it) of the Lord God: such is the glory of the Naam.
O dear one, so many put on many garbs to beg for alms, to fill the belly.
Without devotion to the Lord there is no peace, O mortal; without the Guru, pride does not go.
O dear one, death stands ever over (your) head, the enemy in birth after birth.
Those steeped in the True Shabad are saved; the True Guru has given (them) understanding.
In the Guru's refuge, (Jam's) messenger can neither cast an eye on them nor torment them;
(they) are steeped in the Pure One, the unseen Master, and have fixed their attention on the Fearless.
O dear one, hold the Naam firm, fix your attention on the Naam itself, leaning on the True Guru's support.
Whatever pleases him, that alone he will do; the record of past deeds cannot be erased.
O dear Guru, we have come running to your refuge; no other, no second (support), pleases me.
Now and ever I call on the One alone, the companion from the beginning, from the beginning of the ages.
O dear Lord, keep the honour of your Name; my bond is with you alone.
In your mercy show (me) the sight of the Guru, that Haumai may be burnt away by the Shabad.
O dear Lord, what should I ask for? Nothing is seen to last; whoever has come into this world goes.
Give Nanak the treasure of the Naam, that he may make it the necklace of his heart. ॥8॥
504.2: Raag Gujri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O dear one, we are neither high nor low nor in between; (we are) in the Lord's refuge, the Lord's people.
Steeped in the Naam, we are wholly detached; sorrow, separation and sickness we have cast off.
O brother, devotion to the Master comes by the Guru's grace.
Through the True Guru's word the Pure Lord (dwells) in the heart; (then) there is no subjection to Jam, nor any account left owing to Jam.
With their tongues (the devotees) utter the Lord's praises, in God's company; in whatever pleases the Lord (they rest) in Sahaj.
Without the Lord's Name, life in the world is in vain; without the Lord, even a single moment is fruitless.
O dear one, the false have no place, at home or abroad; the slanderer has no liberation at all.
(Though the slanderer) rages, God does not withdraw his gift; day by day it grows ever more.
O dear one, none can erase the Guru's gift; my Master himself has had it given.
Slanderers, to whom the Guru's gift is not pleasing, have their faces blackened by slander.
O dear one, those who seek (his) refuge God forgives and unites (with himself), without delay of even half a mustard seed.
He is the source of bliss, the Master over the masters; the True Guru unites (one) in union (with him).
O dear one, (whoever) has remembered the ever-merciful (Lord), by his mercy, has had (his) wandering ended by the Guru's teaching.
Touching the paaras, metal turns to gold: (such) is the greatness of the Sat Sangat.
The Lord is the pure water, the mind the bather; (the one to whom) the True Guru is pleasing takes the plunge (in it).
In the company of (the Lord's) servants there is no birth again; (one's) light is merged in the Light.
(O Lord,) you are the great Being, the unreachable tree; we are birds (dwelling) in you.
O Pure One, give Nanak the Naam, that age after age he may praise (you) through the Shabad. ॥8॥
505.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those who worship the True One with loving devotion have a thirst (for him), a supreme love;
weeping and wailing, they make their prayers; in the loving feeling of their hearts they find peace.
O mind, repeat the Naam, (taking) the Lord's refuge.
The Lord's Name is the ship to carry (you) over the world-ocean: make it your life's work.
O mind, death itself wishes well to (one who) dwells on the Lord through the Guru's Shabad.
(For one who) dwells in the mind on the Lord's Name, the intellect knows the Essence, (and finds) the treasure of all good.
Wealth makes the mind fickle and sends it wandering; the world is lost in attachment and fondness (for it).
The Naam (alone) is lasting: (the devotees) make devotion firm in their understanding, and through the Guru's word are steeped in the Shabad.
Wandering, (the world's) doubt does not end; the world wastes away in the sickness of birth (and death).
The Lord is the abode free of (all) desire; the austerity of the Naam is true understanding.
This world is in the grip of attachment and fondness; great is (its) pain of birth and death.
Hasten to the True Guru's refuge, (and) dwell on the Lord's Name in your heart: (so) you will be saved.
(With) the Guru's teaching set unshaken in the mind, the mind takes to reflection on Sahaj.
Pure is that mind in which the True One (dwells); within it is the precious jewel of (divine) knowledge.
In (his) fear and love, through devotion, cross the world-ocean, O mind; fix your mind on the Lord's feet.
(Keep) the Lord's Name, holy and purifying, in your heart, (and say:) this body is in your refuge.
The capital of the Lord's Name in the mind drives off the waves of craving and greed.
Says Nanak: with the mind subdued, (I have come) to your refuge, yours alone, O Pure One. ॥8॥
506.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I dance, and it is this mind that I make dance;
by the Guru's grace I shed my self-centredness.
Whoever keeps the mind steady is set free; whatever I desire, that fruit I obtain.
Dance, O mind, before the Guru.
If you dance to the Guru's will, you will find peace, and at the end the fear of Jam will flee.
The one (the Lord) himself sets dancing is called a devotee; he himself instils his love (in him).
He himself sings, he himself makes (it) heard, and sets this blind mind on the way.
One who dances (so) night and day drives away Shakti (Maya); in the house of Shiv (the Lord) there is no sleep.
In the house of Shakti the world lies asleep; it dances, leaps and sings of other things; the manmukh has no devotion.
Gods and men dance on the side of worldly life, through their deeds; the sages dance, reflecting on knowledge.
Siddhas and seekers who have reflected with understanding through the Guru dance with their attention fixed (on him).
Continents and universes dance in the three qualities; those whose attention is fixed on you, O Lord, dance (too).
All beings and creatures dance; the four sources of life dance.
Those alone dance who please you, (O Lord,) who through the Guru have fixed their attention on the Shabad.
They are the devotees, they know the Essence, whom (the Lord) makes accept his Hukam.
Devotion is this: that the attention stays fixed on the True One; without service there is no devotion.
When one dies while living, then one reflects on the Shabad, and then one finds the True One.
For the sake of Maya many people dance; rare is one who reflects on the Essence.
By the Guru's grace that one alone finds (you), O Lord, on whom your mercy rests.
If the True One is forgotten for a single breath, that time goes to waste.
With every breath he should be cherished ever; he himself forgives, as he wills.
Those alone dance who please you, who through the Guru reflect on the Shabad.
Says Nanak: they find the peace of Sahaj on whom your gracious glance falls. ॥10॥
506.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Without the Lord my soul cannot live, as a child (lives) on the support of milk.
God, unreachable and beyond the senses, is found through the Guru; I am a sacrifice to my True Guru.
O mind, swim across (the world-ocean) through the Lord's praise.
The Amrit-water of the Naam is found through the Guru, (by those) on whom your mercy rests, (O Lord).
Sanak, Sanandan and the sage Narad serve (you); night and day they keep repeating (the Name of) Banwari.
Servants such as Prahlad came to (your) refuge, and (you) kept their honour.
The One, unseen and pure, pervades (all); the one Light of Murari (is in all).
All are beggars, you alone are the Giver; they beg (of you) with hands held out.
The word of the devotees is sublime; they ever sing the wondrous story of the Indescribable.
Their life has borne fruit; they have crossed over themselves and carried their families across.
The manmukhs are in the grip of duality and a corrupt intellect, with the darkness of attachment within them.
They do not care for the discourse of the Sants; they drown along with their families.
The slanderer, by slandering, washes away (others') filth; living on Maya, he is an eater of filth.
Those caught up in slandering the Sants are on neither this shore nor the other.
All this expanse, this play, the Creator has made; the Lord, the Creator, has set his power in it all.
The Lord's one thread runs through the world; (when) he draws the thread out, (only) the One Creator (remains).
With love, with love and relish, (the devotees) sing the Lord's praises; their tongue holds the Lord's sweet essence.
Nanak asks for nothing but the Lord; dear (to him) is the love of the Lord's essence. ॥8॥
507.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Among kings you are called the King; among lords of the land, the Lord of the land.
Among masters yours is the mastery; over all the noble clans, yours is the noblest.
My Father is the great Master, beyond reach.
What praise of you can be offered, O Creator? Beholding (you), we are lost in wonder.
Among the happy you are called the Happy One; above all givers, the Giver.
Among the radiant you are called the Radiant One; among those who savour delights, the one steeped (in delight).
Among heroes you are called the Hero; among enjoyers, the Enjoyer.
Among householders you are the great Householder; among yogis, the Yogi.
Among makers you are called the Maker; among keepers of religious observance, the Observant One.
Among bankers you are the true Banker; among traders, the Trader.
Among courts yours is the Court; of all who shelter those seeking refuge, you are the crowning mark.
How much wealth is yours cannot be counted; I cannot count (your) coins.
Among names, O God, yours is the Name; among the wise, the Wise One.
Among ways of life, O God, yours is the Way; among bathers (at holy places), the Bather.
Among the Siddhas, O God, yours is the siddhi; above all deeds, your deed.
Among all bidding, O God, yours is the bidding; above all commands, your Command.
As you make us speak, so we speak, O Master; what power have we?
In the Saadh Sangat, which is most dear to God, Nanak has sung (his) praise. ॥8॥
508.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Master, Narhar, Kin of the lowly, divine Purifier of the fallen,
Destroyer of fear and dread, Merciful One, Treasure of virtues: fruitful, O Master, is your service.
O Lord, Gopal, great Gobind,
merciful Keshav, (I have come) to the refuge of your feet; carry (me) across the world, the ocean of existence.
Remover of lust and anger, burner of pride and attachment, O Murari, the flower's nectar (makrand) to the mind,
put an end to (my) birth and death, O Upholder of the earth (Dharnidhar); keep (my) honour, O Supreme Bliss.
(We are) burning in the countless waves of Maya; O Lord, (set) the Guru's wisdom as the mantra in (our) hearts.
Cut away (our) proud intellect, O Compassionate One; erase (our) anxiety, O infinite Being.
Remember the Almighty every moment and every instant; meditation on God is the samadhi of Sahaj.
O Merciful to the lowly, ever gracious, all-pervading One: let us beg (of you) the dust of the Saadhs' feet.
Attachment is false, hope ends in evil, desire is full of vice;
keep my faith (safe from them), tear doubt out of (my) mind, and save (me), O Lord, Formless One.
O Lord, those who had not even a cloth (to cover them) become rich and wealthy, with storehouses, through your treasure.
The wicked, the ignorant and the foolish, by your glance, O Sridhar, have become virtuous, wise and steadfast.
Repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world, O mind, and be free while living (jivan mukat); hold faith in (your) heart.
Kindness and compassion to (all) beings, (seeing the Lord) pervading everywhere: this is the way of the supreme swans (Param Hans).
(The Lord) grants the sight of himself, his praise to the ears, the utterance of the Name to the tongue;
the Lord is ever beside (them), close to every limb; O Nanak, God's touch saves the fallen. ॥8॥
508.2: Gujri ki Vaar: by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji); to be sung to the tune of the vaar of Sikandar and Birahim.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This world is dead in the sense of mine; it does not know how to live.
Whoever walks in the Guru's will: such ones attain the state of (true) life.
Those servants live for ever and ever who fix their minds on the Lord's feet.
O Nanak, the Gracious One dwells in (their) minds, and (those) Gurmukhs remain merged in Sahaj. ॥1॥
508.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Within (the self-willed) there is anxiety and pain; they have brought the beating of worldly affairs on their own heads.
Asleep in the love of another, they never wake; their attachment and love are for Maya.
They neither remember the Naam nor reflect on the Shabad: such is the conduct of the manmukh.
They have not found the Name of the Lord and have wasted their life in vain; O Nanak, Jam strikes them and brings them to ruin. ॥2॥
509.1: He brought himself forth; at that time there was no other.
Counsel and deliberation he held with himself alone; what he did came to be.
Then there was neither sky nor underworld, nor the three worlds.
Then the Formless One alone was, by himself; nothing had been brought forth.
As it pleases him, so he does; apart from him there is no other. ॥1॥
509.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My Master is for ever; he is seen by living the Shabad.
He never perishes; he neither comes nor goes.
Let us serve, for ever and ever, the One who pervades all.
Why serve some other, a second, who is born and dies?
Barren is the life of those who, with their minds set on others, do not know their own Master.
O Nanak, there is simply no knowing how great a punishment the Creator deals (them). ॥1॥
509.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let us meditate on the True Name; the True One pervades everything.
O Nanak, one who understands the Hukam and is accepted (in his court) then obtains the true fruit.
(But) one who goes about only talking and speaking, and does not understand the Hukam at all, is blind, wholly unripe. ॥2॥
509.4: He made union and separation, and (so) laid the root of creation.
By his Hukam he fashioned the creation, and blended (his) light into the light (of beings).
From that light alone is all light; this is the Shabad the True Guru has made heard.
Having created Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh, he set them to the work of the three qualities.
He made the root of Maya; (but) peace was found (only) in the fourth state (turiya). ॥2॥
509.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
That alone is japa, that alone is penance, which pleases the True Guru.
Walking in the True Guru's will, one gains glory.
O Nanak, giving up self, such a one merges in the Guru. ॥1॥
509.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Only a rare one takes the Guru's teaching:
O Nanak, the one to whom (the Lord) himself gives (this) glory. ॥2॥
509.7: Attachment to Maya is ignorance, very hard and heavy.
With a heavy load of sins like stones, how is one to swim across?
Those steeped in devotion night and day, the Lord carries across.
Through the Guru's Shabad, casting off Haumai and vice, the mind becomes pure.
Let us meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har; it is the Lord, Har Har, who saves. ॥3॥
509.8: O Kabir, the door of liberation is narrow, a tenth part of a mustard seed;
but the mind has become a maddened elephant: how can it pass through?
If such a True Guru is met, who, well pleased, shows his grace,
then the door of liberation is wide, and I come and go (through it) with ease. ॥1॥
509.9: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, the door of liberation is very small; only one who becomes tiny passes through.
The mind has grown stout with Haumai; how can it go through that (door)?
On meeting the True Guru, Haumai has gone, and the light has come to fill all (within).
(Then) this soul is free for ever, and remains absorbed in Sahaj. ॥2॥
510.1: God, having made the world, has kept it under his own sway.
God is not found by reckoning; (through it one) wanders in the love of another.
On meeting the True Guru one dies while living, and, understanding (the truth), merges in the True One.
Through the Shabad Haumai is shed, and one is joined in union with the Lord.
He knows all, he himself does (all), and he himself delights (in it). ॥4॥
510.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who has not set his mind on the True Guru, in whose mind the Naam has not come to dwell:
cursed is a life like that; what did he gain by coming into this age?
Maya is counterfeit capital; in a moment its false show is stripped away.
Once it is lost from one's hands, the body darkens and the face fades.
In those who have joined their minds to the True Guru, peace has come to dwell.
With love they meditate on the Lord's Name, and keep their loving attention fixed on the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, (the Lord) has entrusted to the True Guru that wealth which abides within his very being;
(whoever receives it from the Guru) is dyed in a deep colour (of love), whose hue grows ever brighter. ॥1॥
510.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Maya has become a she-serpent, coiled about (all) in the world.
Whoever serves her is the very one she then devours.
Some rare Gurmukh is a snake-charmer (gararu); he has crushed and trampled her and put her under his feet.
O Nanak, they alone are saved who keep their loving attention fixed on the True One. ॥2॥
510.4: The bard (dhadhi) cries out and makes God hear (his plea);
within (him) patience grows, and he will find the Perfect One.
As is the writ written from the start, so are the deeds he will do.
When the Master is merciful, he will find (the Lord's) mansion, (his true) home.
That God of mine is very great; through the Guru he will unite (him with himself). ॥5॥
510.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
All (soul-brides) have one Husband, who is always present beside (them).
O Nanak, if she does not obey his Hukam, then though he is within her very home, he is far away.
Those alone will he bring to obey his Hukam on whom his gracious glance falls.
She who has found peace by obeying the Hukam becomes a happy soul-bride, full of love. ॥1॥
510.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
She who did not give her love to her Husband has burned and died all through the night (of life).
O Nanak, the happy soul-brides whose beloved Husband is the Lord, the King, dwell in peace. ॥2॥
510.7: I have wandered over the whole world and seen: the Lord alone is the Giver.
By no device is he found, the Lord who shapes (each) by their deeds.
Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord dwells in the mind, and the Lord is known with ease.
From within, the fire of craving is put out for one who has bathed in the Lord's pool of Amrit.
Great is the glory of the Great One: through the Guru he makes (us) speak (his praise). ॥6॥
510.8: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
What love is this between the body and the swan (the soul), that (the soul) leaves (the body) lying where it falls?
Why speak falsehood to feed it, when it does not go along at the time of departure?
The body is dust, and blind; go and ask the breath (the soul).
(It answers:) I, lured by Maya, come and go again and again;
O Nanak, I did not know the Master's Hukam, through which I might stay merged in the True One. ॥1॥
511.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The wealth of the Naam alone is unshakable; other wealth comes and goes.
No thief can so much as eye this wealth, nor can a snatcher carry it off.
This wealth of the Lord is woven into the soul, and goes along with the soul.
It is obtained from the Perfect Guru; it does not fall into the manmukh's lap.
O Nanak, fortunate are the traders who came here and earned the Naam as their wealth. ॥2॥
511.2: My Master is exceedingly great, the True One, deep and profound.
The whole world is in his power; everything rests on his support.
By the Guru's grace the unshakable, lasting wealth (of his Name) is found.
By (God's) grace the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, (when) the valiant Guru is met.
The virtuous have praised him: the Lord is ever steady, unmoving and perfect. ॥7॥
511.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Cursed is the life of those who cast aside the peace of the Lord and forsake it, and earn pain, committing sins in Haumai.
The ignorant manmukhs are caught in attachment to Maya; no understanding comes to them.
They find no peace in this world or the next; at the end they depart in regret.
If someone meditates on the Naam by the Guru's grace, Haumai leaves him from within.
O Nanak, one for whom it is so written from the first comes and falls at the Guru's feet. ॥1॥
511.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is an upturned lotus; in him is neither devotion nor the Name.
He moves within Shakti (Maya), and falsehood is all his striving.
His inner being and his mind are not softened (by love), and from his mouth come insipid words.
Such people, though joined to righteousness, do not blend with it, for within them is falsehood and self-interest.
O Nanak, the Creator has made this design: the manmukhs drown, speaking falsehood again and again, and the Gurmukhs cross over, repeating the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
511.5: Without understanding (that he is found by the Guru's grace), one falls into the great round (of births), and comes and goes again.
One who has not served the True Guru departs at the end in regret.
When (God) grants his grace, the Guru is found, and one loses self-conceit from within.
The thirst and hunger (for Maya) are lifted from within, and peace comes and settles in the mind.
(Then) one praises (God) for ever and ever, with the heart's attention fixed (on him). ॥8॥
511.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who serves his own True Guru is revered by everyone.
Above all means is this means: that the Lord's Name is obtained.
(Through the Name) coolness and calm dwell within; repeating (it), there is peace in the heart for ever.
The Amrit (of the Name) becomes (his) food, the Amrit (his) clothing; O Nanak, the Name becomes (his) glory. ॥1॥
511.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O mind, listen to the Guru's teaching, and you will find the Lord, the treasure of virtues.
The Lord, the giver of peace, will dwell in the mind, and Haumai and pride will go.
O Nanak, (God) is found through his glance of grace; then the attention stays fixed (on him) night and day. ॥2॥
512.1: The Gurmukh is made pure: (he gains) truth and contentment, and (sees) the True One everywhere.
Deceit and vice have gone from within him, and he has conquered his mind with ease.
There the Light shines forth, the relish of bliss (is tasted), and ignorance is destroyed.
Night and day he utters the Lord's virtues, and (those) virtues are made manifest (in him).
(He knows that) the Giver of all is One; the Lord alone is the Friend. ॥9॥
512.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who knows Brahm (God) is the one to be called a Brahmin: one who keeps his attention fixed on the Lord night and day.
He seeks the True Guru's counsel, practises truth and self-restraint, and his disease of Haumai departs.
He sings the Lord's virtues, gathers virtues, and keeps his light merged in the Light.
In this age rare is the Brahm Giani (one who knows God), who erases Haumai and merges (in God).
O Nanak, by meeting one who meditates on the Lord's Name night and day, lasting peace is found. ॥1॥
512.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Within the ignorant manmukh is deceit, and with his tongue he speaks falsehood.
The Lord, the Purakh, is not won over when deceit is practised; as his very nature, he sees and hears (all) at all times.
In the love of another he goes and instructs the world, out of self-interest, for the poison of Maya and attachment.
Living this way he suffers pain for ever; he is born and he dies, and comes and goes again.
His dread never ends at all; he burns and is consumed in filth.
The one on whom my Lord shows grace, he has him hear the Guru's teaching.
(Such a one) meditates on the Lord's Name, sings only the Lord's Name, and the Lord's Name alone sets (him) free at the end. ॥2॥
512.4: Those whom (God) has made to obey his Hukam are the perfect ones in the world.
They serve their Master, reflecting on the perfect Shabad.
The Lord's service and attendance (are done) through love of the true Shabad.
They have attained the Lord's mansion who have killed Haumai within.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs stay united (with him), repeating the Lord's Name and keeping it in the heart. ॥10॥
512.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the Gurmukh wells up the strain of focused attention and of Sahaj; he has fixed his mind on the true Name.
The Gurmukh stays dyed in (the Lord's) love night and day; the Lord's Name is pleasing to his mind.
The Gurmukhs behold the Lord, the Gurmukhs utter (the praise of) the Lord, the Gurmukhs, in Sahaj, have set their love on the Lord.
O Nanak, the Gurmukh gains true knowledge, and the deep darkness of ignorance is driven away.
The one on whom perfect grace rests from the first: that Gurmukh has meditated on the Lord's Name. ॥1॥
512.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have not served the True Guru, who have not come to love the Shabad,
who have not meditated on the Name in Sahaj: what did they come into the world for?
Again and again they are cast into births, and are ever wretched in filth.
Attached to false greed, they reach neither this shore nor the far shore.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs are saved, whom the Creator himself has united (with himself). ॥2॥
513.1: The devotees look beautiful at the True One's door, held steady there by the true Shabad.
Love for the Lord has sprung up in them; the Lord's love draws them.
They remain in the Lord's love, ever dyed in (his) love, and (their) tongues drink the Lord's sweet essence.
Fruitful is the birth of those who have known the dear Lord through the Guru and enshrined him in the heart.
Without the Guru (the world) wanders wailing, led astray by the love of another. ॥11॥
513.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Kalyug the Name is the treasure; (one who) has earned it through devotion has attained the highest state, (union with) the Lord.
Serving the True Guru, (he) has enshrined the Lord's Name in the mind, and meditated on the Name night and day.
By the Guru's word he is detached in the very midst of the household; he has burnt away Haumai and attachment.
He has crossed over himself and has carried the whole world across; blessed is the mother who bore him.
Such a True Guru is found only by one on whose forehead the Lord has written it from the first.
Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to his Guru, who set him, astray in doubt, on the path. ॥1॥
513.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Seeing Maya of the three qualities, (people) have gone astray, as the moth, seeing the lamp, is burnt up in its flame.
The pandits, straying again and again, keep their eyes on Maya: let us see whether someone has brought something and offered it.
In the love of another they read every day only of Maya, the poison; God has led them away from the Name.
The yogis, the jangams and the sannyasis too have gone astray; their egotism and pride have grown great.
They will not accept clothing and food given as alms in good faith; through the stubbornness of their minds they have wasted their lives.
Among all these, that person alone has reached the steady state who has meditated on the Name through the Guru.
O servant Nanak, to whom can one say this and make it heard, when all act as (the Lord) makes them act? ॥2॥
513.4: Attachment to Maya is a ghost, (and so are) lust, anger and egotism.
These are all Jam's subjects; over them falls Jam's hard rod.
The manmukhs, to whom the love of another is dear, are put on Jam's road.
In the city of Jam they are bound and beaten, and no one hears (their) cries.
One on whom (God) shows grace meets the Guru; through the Guru comes release (from them). ॥12॥
513.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Haumai and possessiveness are an enchantress who has devoured the manmukhs.
Those who fix their minds on attachment to another, she has seized and clings to them.
If she is burnt away through the Guru's Shabad, then she leaves from within.
(Then) body and mind become bright, and the Name comes to dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, the remedy that kills (the poison of) Maya is the Lord's Name; it is obtained through the Guru. ॥1॥
513.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This mind has wandered for so many ages; it does not stay steady, and keeps coming and going.
It pleased the Lord, and so he made it wander, fashioning the deceiving world and bringing forth this play.
When the Lord forgives, then (it) meets the Guru, and stays steady, merged (in God).
O Nanak, through the mind itself the mind has been won over; (now) nothing dies and nothing is born. ॥2॥
514.1: The body is a boundless fortress, obtained only by good fortune.
Within the body (God) himself dwells; he himself is the enjoyer of its pleasures.
(Yet) he himself is detached and untouched; the Lord is free of all ties and yet joined (with all).
Whatever pleases him, he does; what the Lord does, that comes to pass.
Meditate on the Lord's Name through the Guru, and the separations (from God) are lifted. ॥13॥
514.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The True One himself has (us) say Waah Waah, through the Guru's Shabad.
Waah Waah is (his) praise and glory; rare is the one who understands (this) through the Guru.
The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the True One; (through it) comes union with the True One.
O Nanak, saying Waah Waah, God is found; (yet this praise) is obtained by his grace. ॥1॥
514.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The tongue that says Waah Waah is made beautiful by the Shabad.
Through the perfect Shabad, God has come and been met.
From the mouths of the very fortunate, (God) has Waah Waah brought forth.
Those who say Waah Waah are the beautiful ones; the people come to worship them.
Waah Waah is obtained by (God's) grace; O Nanak, (through it) honour is won at the True Door. ॥2॥
514.4: In the body-fortress of the proud are hard (adamantine) doors of falsehood and deceit.
The blind, ignorant manmukhs, deluded by doubt, do not see (these doors).
By no means are (they) found; those who wear religious garb have worn themselves out with their garbs.
Through the Guru's Shabad (the doors) are opened (for those) who repeat the Lord's Name.
The dear Lord is a tree of Amrit; those who have drunk (its Amrit) are satisfied. ॥14॥
514.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Saying Waah Waah, the night (of life) passes in peace.
Saying Waah Waah, there is bliss for ever, O my mother.
Saying Waah Waah, the attention is fixed on the Lord.
Only by (God's) grace does (one) say Waah Waah, as (he himself) has it said.
O Nanak, Waah Waah comes only by the True One's will. ॥1॥
514.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the True One; the Gurmukh has searched and found it.
Through the Shabad he utters Waah Waah, and Waah Waah with his heart.
Saying Waah Waah, the Gurmukh has searched with ease and found the Lord.
O Nanak, very fortunate are they who keep the Lord, Har Har, cherished in their hearts. ॥2॥
514.7: O greedy mind, so very greedy, you are ever steeped in greed.
Longing for enticing Maya, you roam in all ten directions.
Hereafter, (your) name and caste will not go (with you); as a manmukh you suffer pain.
With your tongue you have not tasted the Lord's sweet essence, and you speak insipid words.
Those who have tasted the Amrit (of the Name) through the Guru are satisfied. ॥15॥
514.8: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let us say Waah Waah to the One who is true, deep and profound;
let us say Waah Waah to the One who is the giver of virtues, steady in understanding;
let us say Waah Waah to the One who pervades all;
let us say Waah Waah to the One who brings sustenance to all.
O Nanak, knowing him as the One alone, let us praise with Waah Waah him whom the True Guru has shown (us). ॥1॥
515.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukhs ever say Waah Waah; the manmukhs eat poison and die.
Waah Waah does not please them; (their life) passes in sorrow upon sorrow.
Through the Guru, Amrit is (their) drink; with loving attention fixed, they say Waah Waah.
O Nanak, the servants who say Waah Waah are pure; they gain understanding of the three worlds. ॥2॥
515.2: By the Lord's will the Guru is met, and one's service and devotion take shape;
by the Lord's will the Lord dwells in the mind, and the essence (of the Name) is drunk in Sahaj;
by the Lord's will peace is found, and the Lord's profit is earned every day;
(one) is seated on the Lord's throne, and dwells for ever in one's own home (within).
They alone have accepted the Lord's will who have met the Guru. ॥16॥
515.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those servants ever say Waah Waah whom (God) himself gives understanding.
Saying Waah Waah, the mind becomes pure, and Haumai leaves from within.
The Gursikh who says Waah Waah every day obtains the fruit the mind longs for.
Beautiful are the servants who say Waah Waah; O Lord, join (me) to their company,
that within my heart I may utter Waah Waah, and say Waah Waah with my mouth as well.
To those who say Waah Waah, Nanak offers his body and mind. ॥1॥
515.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Waah Waah! The Master is true, whose Name is Amrit.
Whoever has served (him) has obtained the fruit; I am a sacrifice to them.
Waah Waah! He is the treasure of virtues; only the one to whom he gives (it) partakes of it.
Waah Waah! He fills the waters and the land; through the Guru he is found.
O Gursikhs, all of you, say Waah Waah every day; Waah Waah is pleasing to the Perfect Guru.
O Nanak, whoever says Waah Waah in mind and heart, Jam's servant does not come near him. ॥2॥
515.5: The dear Lord is true, ever true; true is the Guru's Bani.
Through the True Guru the True One is recognised, and (one's attention) merges in the True One, in Sahaj.
(Such ones) keep awake night and day and never sleep; the night (of their life) goes by as they keep awake.
Those who have tasted the Lord's sweet essence through the Guru's teaching are blessed beings.
Without the Guru no one has found (him); the ignorant have wasted away and died. ॥17॥
515.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Bani of Waah Waah is (the form of) the Formless One; none other is as great as he.
Waah Waah! He is unreachable and fathomless; Waah Waah! He alone is true.
Waah Waah! He is free of all care; Waah Waah! What he does comes to pass.
Waah Waah! The Name is Amrit; some rare one obtains it through the Guru.
Waah Waah is obtained by (God's) grace; he himself gives (it) in his mercy.
O Nanak, Waah Waah is obtained through the Guru; (the one who obtains it) takes the Name night and day. ॥1॥
516.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without serving the True Guru, peace does not come; there is no other place (to find it).
However much one may long, without (his) grace (he) cannot be found.
Those within whom is the vice of greed are led astray in the love of another.
Their birth and death do not end; in Haumai they suffer pain.
Of those who have fixed their minds on the True Guru, not one is left empty.
They are not summoned by Jam, nor do they suffer pain.
O Nanak, through the Guru they are saved; they merge in the True Shabad. ॥2॥
516.2: Only the one who holds love for the Master should be called a bard;
standing at (his) door he serves, and reflects through the Guru's Shabad.
The bard who keeps the True One enshrined in his heart will reach (the Master's) door and home.
Lofty is the bard's dwelling, through love for the Lord's Name.
The bard's service and duty (is this): he repeats (the Name of) the Lord, and the Lord carries him across. ॥18॥
516.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When a Gujri, a woman of rustic caste, finds her own Husband,
(it is) by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad and repeating the Lord's Name night and day.
She whom the True Guru meets is filled with the fear (of God); that woman is of noble family.
She alone on whom the Creator has shown grace recognises the Hukam of her Husband.
That (other) one, without good ways and of ill traits, the Husband has cast off and left.
When the fear (of God) takes hold, the filth (of the mind) is cut away and the body becomes pure.
There is light within and the understanding becomes noble, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, the deep ocean of virtues.
She sits in the fear (of God), she lives in the fear, and in the fear she does her work.
Here (she has) peace and honours, and in the Lord's court the door of liberation.
Through the fear, the Fearless One is found, and (her) light merges in the boundless Light.
O Nanak, she who pleases the Master is the good one: she on whom the Creator himself bestows his grace. ॥1॥
516.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Let us praise (him) for ever and ever; I am a sacrifice to the True One.
O Nanak, let that tongue burn which forsakes the One and clings to another. ॥2॥
516.5: He created the partial incarnations, and he made the love of another.
As kings rule their kingdoms, (so they ruled), and fought over pain and pleasure.
Shiva and Brahma serve (him), yet they did not find his end.
The Fearless, Formless One is beyond all sight; he is revealed through the Guru.
There, sorrow and separation do not touch; (such a one) becomes steady in the world. ॥19॥
516.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
All this, as much form as there is, is coming and going.
Whoever has written this account (in the mind) has been approved.
O Nanak, whoever sets himself up (as great) is a fool, an ignorant one. ॥1॥
516.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The mind is an elephant, the Guru its driver, and (the Guru's) wisdom the goad; wherever (the driver) pulls, there it goes.
O Nanak, an elephant without the goad strays into the wilderness again and again. ॥2॥
516.8: My prayer is offered to him who created (all).
By serving my own True Guru, I have received every fruit.
I have meditated always on the Lord's Name, the Amrit;
in the company of the Sants I have erased (my) pain.
Nanak has become free of care, having secured the Lord's imperishable wealth. ॥20॥
517.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the field the embankments are high, with an eye on the high house, the cloud;
(so) when devotion is at home in the bride, the Friend comes (to her) as a guest.
O cloud, if you are to rain, rain (now); why would you rain afterwards?
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who, through the Guru, have found (the Lord) within the mind. ॥1॥
517.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Sweet is what pleases; a friend is one who is true and straight.
O Nanak, (this) is understood through the Guru by the one in whom (God) himself makes light. ॥2॥
517.3: This is the servant's prayer before God: (O Lord,) you are the true Master.
You are the protector for ever and ever; I meditate on you.
Every being and creature is yours; you pervade them all.
Whoever slanders your servant, you strike him down and destroy him.
O Nanak, give up worry and stay free of care, clinging to (the Lord's) feet. ॥21॥
517.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Hoping and hoping, the world has died, yet hope neither dies nor departs.
O Nanak, hopes are fulfilled by fixing the mind on the True One. ॥1॥
517.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Hope and desire will die (only when) he who made them takes them away.
O Nanak, nothing is lasting except the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
517.6: He himself created the world, giving it a complete design.
The Lord himself is the banker, himself the trader, and himself the shop.
He himself is the ocean and the ship, and he himself the boatman.
He himself is the Guru and himself the disciple; he himself shows the landing-place (on the far shore).
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Naam, and cut away all sins.
517.7: Raag Gujri Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
To dwell on the Guru within, and with the tongue to repeat the Guru's Name;
to behold the True Guru with the eyes, and with the ears to hear the Guru's Name;
steeped in (the love of) the True Guru, one finds a place in the Lord's court.
Says Nanak, (God) gives this gift to the one on whom he shows grace;
such ones are counted the best in the world, but they are rare, a very few. ॥1॥
517.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whom the Protector protected, he himself has rescued;
placing (them) at the Guru's feet, he has set their affairs right.
He himself became merciful and did not put them out of his mind;
in the company of the holy, he carried them across the world-ocean.
The Saakats (those who have turned from God), the slanderers and the wicked he destroyed in an instant.
In Nanak's mind is the support of that Master,
remembering whom there is peace, and all sorrows go. ॥2॥
518.1: (O Lord,) you are without lineage, stainless, the all-pervading Being, unreachable and boundless.
You are true, wholly true; you are seen to be true, ever true.
Nothing of what you have established seems false.
The Giver gives to all, as many as he has created.
Stringing (all) on a single thread, he has set his light (in them).
By (his) Hukam (beings are) in the world-ocean; by (his) Hukam (they) are carried across.
O dear God, he alone meditates on you who has good fortune (written) on his forehead.
Your state and extent cannot be perceived; I am a sacrifice to you. ॥1॥
518.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, you come to dwell in the mind, unsought;
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, (we) find the nine treasures in (our own) home;
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, then (we) live by the Guru's mantra;
O Merciful One, when you are pleased, then, O Nanak, (we) merge in the True One. ॥1॥
518.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Many sit on (royal) seats, and sound a great many instruments;
O Nanak, without the True Name the honour of none has lasted. ॥2॥
518.4: (O God,) the Vedas, along with the Kateb, stand and meditate on you;
those who lie at your door are beyond all counting.
The Brahmas meditate on you, and the Indras on their thrones;
Shiva, Vishnu and the incarnations utter the Lord's praise with their mouths;
so do the pirs, the prophets, the sheikhs, the elders and the saints (auliya).
O Formless Lord, woven through all like warp and weft, you blossom in every heart.
Through falsehood one works one's own ruin; through righteousness one stands firm.
To whatever you yourself attach (us), to that alone we are attached. ॥2॥
518.5: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The heedless one) is lazy in doing good, and bold as a lion in doing evil.
O Nanak, today or tomorrow the heedless one's foot will be caught in the noose (of death). ॥1॥
518.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
However many (my) wrong ways, (your) love does not stay hidden.
Says Nanak: you, my Husband Lord, the true Friend within the mind, have covered (them). ॥2॥
518.7: O Merciful One, I ask this of you: make me the slave of your servants.
I obtain the nine treasures and a kingdom; by uttering (your Name) I live.
The treasure of the Amrit Naam is plentiful in the homes of (your) servants.
In their company I am delighted, hearing (your) praise with my ears.
I do their service, and (my) body is made pure.
Waving the fan, (carrying) water, grinding (the corn) and washing (their) feet, I rejoice.
By myself nothing can be done; O God, look on (me) with your glance of grace,
and let me, who have no virtue, be given a place in the dharamsal (house of worship) of the Sants. ॥3॥
518.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Friend, may I ever remain the dust of your feet.
In your refuge, may Nanak see you ever present. ॥1॥
518.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Countless fallen ones become pure when (their) mind is attached to the Lord's feet.
God's Name is the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage; O Nanak, (it comes to the one) on whose forehead good fortune is (written). ॥2॥
518.10: With every breath and every morsel, let the Name of the Sustainer be repeated always.
The one on whom he shows mercy, he does not forget.
It is he who creates, and he himself who destroys.
The Knower knows everything; understanding, he gives it thought.
In an instant he sets up the creation in countless forms.
The one he joins to the Truth, him he saves.
The one on whose side he stands never loses.
His court stands forever, never broken; I bow to him. ॥4॥
519.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lust, anger and greed should be given up; let them be burned in the fire.
O Nanak, while we live, let us repeat the True Name every day. ॥1॥
519.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering his God again and again, he has obtained all the fruits;
O Nanak, the one who has worshipped the Naam has been united (with God) by the Perfect Guru. ॥2॥
519.3: He is liberated (while living) in the world, whom the Guru has instructed.
His affliction is gone, (his) anxieties are erased.
Beholding the sight of him, the world is delighted.
In the company of (God's) servant one is delighted, the filth of sins washed away.
There the True Name, the Amrit, is repeated.
The mind finds contentment, and the hungry one is satisfied.
The one in whose heart the Name has come to dwell has his bonds cut away.
By the Guru's grace, only some rare one earns the wealth of the Lord. ॥5॥
519.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In my mind I think this thought: that I should rise each day and make the effort;
O Lord, Friend of Nanak, give (me) the occupation of the Lord's Kirtan. ॥1॥
519.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whom God has kept safe by casting his glance (of grace): their mind and body are dyed in the Primal Lord.
O Nanak, (so it is with) those who are pleasing to God; I, poor one, am dying in pain. ॥2॥
519.6: Whatever pain there is in your heart, lay it before the Guru in prayer;
give up all your cleverness, and offer up your mind and body (to him).
Worship the Guru's feet, and evil-mindedness burns away.
In the company of the holy, cross the terrible world-ocean.
Serve the True Guru, the divine one; you will not die of fear in the hereafter.
In an instant he brings delight, filling the empty to the brim.
The mind finds contentment when the Lord is meditated on always.
He alone takes up the True Guru's service on whom (God's) grace rests from the very beginning. ॥6॥
519.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(My love) is fixed in the right place; the Joiner has joined it.
O Nanak, the other waves number hundreds of thousands, (but) my Beloved does not let (me) drown. ॥1॥
519.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the dreadful forest I have found one companion: the Lord's Name, the remover of pain.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the beloved Sants; (through them) Nanak's tasks are fulfilled. ॥2॥
519.9: All treasures are obtained by being dyed in your love.
Repeating your (Name), there is no regret.
No one can reach (the standing of) your servants, who lean on you.
Praise, praise to the Perfect Guru! Remembering (him) in the mind, I find peace.
The treasure of praise is with the Guru; it is obtained by (God's) grace.
When the True Guru looks (on one) with his glance of grace, there is no more wandering.
The Merciful One himself protects (them), making them his own servants.
I live by hearing, again and again, the Name of the Lord, Har Har Har Har. ॥7॥
520.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You, my Husband Lord, have given (me) the silk robe of love to keep my honour covered.
My Master is wise and all-seeing; Nanak does not know your worth. ॥1॥
520.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through remembering you I have found everything; I have seen no hardship.
O Nanak, the one whose honour the True Master keeps, no one can erase (it). ॥2॥
520.3: Great peace comes when the Merciful Lord is meditated on;
heaps of diseases are destroyed when the Lord's praises are sung;
coolness pervades within when God comes to mind;
hope is fulfilled when the Name is enshrined in the mind.
No obstacle comes in the way when self-conceit is lost;
the treasure of divine wisdom (comes) when understanding is received from the Guru.
He alone has obtained all things to whom (God) himself has had them given.
(O God,) you are the Master of all; all are in your shelter. ॥8॥
520.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As I cross the (world-) river, my foot does not sink (in the mire), for within me is love for you.
O Husband Lord, I have stitched my heart to your feet; for Nanak, the Lord is the raft and the boat. ॥1॥
520.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those at whose sight evil-mindedness departs: they alone are our friends.
I search the whole world; O servant Nanak, (such friends) are a rare few. ॥2॥
520.6: (O God,) seeing your devotees, the Master comes to mind;
dwelling in the Saadh Sangat, the mind's filth is cut away;
repeating the Shabad of (God's) servant, the fear of birth and death is cut away.
The Sants untie the bonds, and all the demons run and hide.
They attach (our) love to him who upholds all (creation),
the unreachable, the infinite, whose seat is the highest of the high.
With palms joined, day and night, he should be meditated on with every breath.
When he himself becomes merciful, then the company of the devotees is found. ॥9॥
520.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the alien wilds there is stifling heat and turmoil, and cries ring out on the roads.
O Husband Lord, my cord is tied to you; (so) Nanak passes through the forest in bliss. ॥1॥
520.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
True fellowship is with those in whose company the Name is repeated.
O Nanak, no company should be kept with those who care (only) for their own ends. ॥2॥
520.9: Approved is that moment in which the True Guru is met.
When the company of the Saadh is found, pain does not strike again.
The unshakeable place is found, and one does not lie in the womb again.
The One, Brahm, is seen in all.
The essence of wisdom (comes) by fixing the attention (on God) and drawing the gaze in (from outward things).
It is all the repetition of (God's Name), whatever is spoken by the mouth.
Understanding the Hukam, one is delighted, and dwells in peace upon peace.
Those whom (God) has tested and placed in (his) treasury are never counterfeit again. ॥10॥
520.10: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The pangs of separation are pincers (of torture), so harsh they cannot be borne.
If that Master is met, O Nanak, then truly (there is) every comfort. ॥1॥
521.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The earth dwells in water; wood keeps fire (within it).
O Nanak, (such) is that Husband Lord, on whose support everyone rests. ॥2॥
521.2: (O God,) the works you have done are within your power alone;
that alone comes to pass in the world which you have ordained from the very start.
We are struck with wonder and awe, seeing your creation.
(We,) your servants, have fallen at your refuge; be gracious, that I may be set free.
The treasure is in your hands; you give it to the one who pleases you.
Those on whom (you) become merciful, they alone receive the Lord's Name.
O unreachable, imperceptible, infinite (Lord), your end cannot be found.
The one on whom you are gracious meditates on the Naam. ॥11॥
521.3: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The ladles move about (in the food) but do not know its taste; they stay empty.
Those faces alone look (lovely), O Nanak, that are dyed in the relish of love. ॥1॥
521.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the tracker (the Guru) I have traced the footprints (of those who) had laid (my field) waste.
You, my Husband Lord, have given (it) a fence; O Nanak, the field is not laid waste (now). ॥2॥
521.5: Worship that True One, in whose keeping is everything.
He himself is the Master of both ends (this world and the next), and in an instant he sets (all affairs) right.
Give up all (other) devices, and take hold of his shelter;
run and fall into his refuge, and gain the joy of all joys.
(Good) deeds, dharam and the knowledge of the essence: (all) come with the company of the Sants;
when the Amrit Naam is repeated, no obstacle stands in the way.
The one to whom he himself is kind: in that one's mind he comes to dwell;
when the Master is pleased, all treasures are obtained. ॥12॥
521.6: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have found the One worth finding, for my Beloved has shown grace.
There is one Creator alone; O Nanak, no second is seen. ॥1॥
521.7: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Drawing the arrow of Truth, throw down the wretched sins;
keep the Guru's sweet mantra in mind, O Nanak, and sorrow will not come. ॥2॥
521.8: Praise, praise to the Creator, who himself has brought cool peace.
Always repeat (the Name of) him who is kind to all beings and creatures.
The Mighty One has shown mercy, and the wailing and lament are over;
fevers, sorrows and diseases have fled, through the glory of the perfect Guru.
Honouring the lowly and setting them firm, he has given (them) his own protection;
he himself has set (them) free, cutting away all bonds.
Craving is quenched, hope is fulfilled, the mind is sated with contentment.
The boundless Master is the greatest of the great; neither virtue nor sin leaves a stain on him. ॥13॥
521.9: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those on whom God becomes merciful, they alone repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har.
O Nanak, as soon as they meet the Saadh Sangat, their love is drawn to Ram. ॥1॥
521.10: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remember Ram, O fortunate ones; he is in the water, on the land and in the sky.
O Nanak, when the Name is worshipped, no obstacle stands in the way. ॥2॥
521.11: What the devotees say is approved; it finds acceptance in the Lord's court.
(O Lord,) your devotees lean on you; they are dyed in the True Name.
The one to whom he is merciful: that one's pain departs.
O Merciful One, the devotees are your own; you bestow your kindness on them.
Pain, suffering, grave disease and Maya do not touch such a one.
This is the devotees' support: they sing the praises of Govind;
for ever and ever, day and night, meditating on the One alone,
and drinking the Amrit Naam, (the Lord's) servants remain sated with the Naam. ॥14॥
522.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Millions of obstacles beset the one who forgets the Name;
O Nanak, (such people) wail night and day, like a crow in a deserted house. ॥1॥
522.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When union with the Beloved comes about, that alone is the lovely season.
May he not be forgotten for a moment or an instant; O Nanak, let him be remembered always. ॥2॥
522.3: (The five vices) are brave warriors and heroes, whom no one has held back;
the five have gathered a mighty, stubborn army;
the ten women (the organs) make even ascetics who have renounced the world cling (to pleasures);
conquering (all) one by one, they take them into their own ranks: this alone is what they want.
(The world of) the three qualities is in their power; no one has turned them back.
Doubt is (their) fort and Maya the moat: say, by what means can it be broken?
By worshipping the perfect Guru this fearsome army is smashed.
Before him I would stand day and night with joined hands. ॥15॥
522.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sing (his) praises day after day, and all sins are washed away;
O Nanak, if the Name is forgotten, millions of torments spring up. ॥1॥
522.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, when the True Guru is met, the way (of life) becomes perfect;
(then,) while laughing, playing, dressing and eating, liberation comes in the very midst (of it all). ॥2॥
522.6: Blessed, blessed is that True Guru, who has torn down the fort of doubt.
Praise, praise to that True Guru, who has joined (us) to the Lord.
The Guru gives the Naam, the treasure that never runs out, as medicine;
it is he who has destroyed the great and dreadful disease.
The treasure of the Naam is found, a vast store of riches;
this priceless (human) birth is won, and one's own self is recognised.
The greatness of the mighty Guru, the Divine One, cannot be told;
the Guru is the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, beyond the farthest beyond, unseen and unfathomable. ॥16॥
522.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Making the effort, live (the true life); practising (it), enjoy peace;
meditating, meet God; O Nanak, (so) anxiety is lifted. ॥1॥
522.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Good thoughts, the uttering of Gobind's praises, the pure company of the Saadh (be mine);
have mercy, O Lord, that I, Nanak, may not forget the Naam for even a moment. ॥2॥
522.9: (O Lord,) if (all) that happens is your doing, why should we be afraid?
The one meeting whom the Name is repeated: to that one let (our) soul be offered.
When the Master beyond count comes to mind, (the heart) is filled with joy.
Who can harm the one on whose side the Formless Lord stands?
Everything is in his power; no one is outside (it).
That (Lord) has come to dwell in the minds of the devotees; through Truth he is absorbed (in them).
Your servants meditate on you; you are (their) Protector.
Almighty over all, you make (them) glad with your glance of grace. ॥17॥
523.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) take away lust, anger, intoxication (of pride), greed, attachment and evil desires;
keep (me) safe, O my own God; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥1॥
523.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Eating and eating, the mouth has worn out; wearing (clothes), the whole body (too);
O Nanak, cursed is the life of those whose love has not been fixed on the True One. ॥2॥
523.3: As your Hukam is, just so it has to be;
wherever you yourself keep (us), there (we) must go and stand.
In the love of your Name, evil-mindedness is washed away;
repeating you over and over, O Formless Lord, doubt and fear are cast away.
Those who are dyed in your love are not yoked to births (again);
within and without, their eyes behold the One.
Those who have recognised the Hukam never have to weep;
O Nanak, they string the Name, (God's) gift, into their minds. ॥18॥
523.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
While alive he did not remember (the Lord); dead, he mingles with the dust;
O Nanak, the foolish and unclean Saakat has passed (his life) with the world. ॥1॥
523.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The one who) remembered the Lord while living, and in dying (stayed) in the Lord's love,
has carried the precious gift of birth across, O Nanak, in the company of the Saadh. ॥2॥
523.6: From the beginning, from the start of the ages, (God) himself is the Protector;
the Creator's Name is True, and the True One pervades (all).
Nowhere is he lacking; he fills every single heart.
Merciful and mighty, he himself makes (us) do the labour (of devotion).
Those in whose minds he himself has come to dwell are at ease for ever.
Having made the creation himself, he himself has cherished it;
he himself is everything, endless and boundless.
With the support of the perfect Guru, Nanak has kept (him) in remembrance. ॥19॥
523.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the beginning, in the middle and at the end, the Supreme God has protected (his servant);
the True Guru has given (him) the Lord's Name, and (he) has tasted the Amrit.
(His is) the boundless company of the Saadhs, and night and day he dwells on the Lord's virtues;
he has gained every wish of his heart, and does not wander through births.
All lies in the Creator's hands, who brings about (every) cause.
Nanak begs for this gift: that by the dust (of the feet) of the Sants he may cross over. ॥1॥
523.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Enshrine in your mind the One who created (you).
Whichever servant has meditated on the Master has found peace;
that Gurmukh's life has borne fruit, and his coming (into the world) is accepted.
Understanding the Hukam, he is in bliss: (the Hukam) the Master has decreed.
The one to whom (God) himself has become merciful does not wander in doubt;
whatever the Master has given, he has found it to be joy.
O Nanak, the one to whom the Friend is kind, he makes (him) understand the Hukam;
those whom he himself leads astray die over and over and are ever born again. ॥2॥
523.9: (God) struck down the slanderers at once, and did not let them stand for even an instant.
God cannot bear (his) servant's pain: seizing (the slanderers), he has yoked them to births.
By the hair of their foreheads he has dashed them down, and cast them on the road of Jam.
Struck by pain, they cry out, and lie in dreadful hell.
Hugging (his) servants to his breast, O Nanak, the True Lord has kept them safe. ॥20॥
524.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat (the Name of) Ram, O fortunate ones; he fills the water and the land.
O Nanak, when the Name is meditated on, no obstacle stands in the way. ॥1॥
524.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Millions of obstacles beset the one who forgets the Name;
O Nanak, (such people) wail night and day, like a crow in a deserted house. ॥2॥
524.3: Remembering the Giver over and over, (my) heart's aims are fulfilled;
the wish and the hope of the mind are fulfilled, and the sorrows are gone.
The treasure of the Naam is found, which (I) was seeking;
(my) light has merged with the Light, and the toil is over.
In that house peace, Sahaj and bliss have come to dwell;
coming and going have ended; there is no birth there, nor death.
Master and servant are seen to be one and the same;
by the Guru's grace, Nanak has merged in the True One.
524.4: Raag Gujri, the hymns of the Bhagats.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Ghar 2, a Chaupada of Sri Kabir Ji.
With four feet and two horns, and a mouth that cannot speak, how then will you sing of (the Lord's) virtues?
Whether you rise or sit, the stick will fall on you; where then will you hide your head?
Without the Lord, you will become an ox in another's hands,
with torn nostrils and broken shoulders, eating the chaff of kodo millet.
Roaming the forest all day long, even then your belly will not be full.
You do not heed what the devotees, the Lord's servants, tell you; you will reap what you yourself have done.
Going through pain and pleasure, sunk in great delusion, you will wander through countless births.
You have thrown away the jewel of (human) life and forgotten God; where will you find this chance again?
Going round and round like an oil-presser's ox, the night (of your life) will pass without release.
Says Kabir: without the Name of Ram, you will beat your head and regret. ॥4॥
524.5: Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Kabir's mother weeps, sobbing again and again:
O Raghurai (the Lord), how will these children live?
Kabir has left off all his work, the setting of the warp and the weaving,
and has written the Lord's Name upon his body.
Kabir answers: as long as I am running the thread through the eye of the bobbin,
so long does Ram, the Beloved, slip from my mind.
My understanding is shallow, and by caste I am a weaver,
(yet) the Lord's Name is the profit I have gained.
Says Kabir: listen, O my mother:
for us and for these (children) the Giver is the one Raghurai. ॥4॥
525.1: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Pade of Sri Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O Lord,) if you give (me) a kingdom, what glory is that (to me)?
If you make me beg for alms, what would I lose?
O my mind, worship the Lord, (in whom is) the state of nirban;
your coming and going will not happen again.
(O Lord,) you created all, and you have led all astray in doubt;
the one to whom you give (it), that one alone has understanding.
If the True Guru is met, doubt goes.
Whom shall I worship? No other comes into my sight.
One stone is treated with love,
(and) on another stone the foot is set.
If that one is a god, then this one too is a god.
Says Namdev: as for me, (I am in) the Lord's service. ॥4॥
525.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
No stain of dirt is on him; he is beyond all dirt; like a fragrance, he has come and settled (in every heart), O sister.
No one saw him coming; who can know (him), O sister?
Who can describe him? By whom can he be understood? The beautiful Lord (Ramaiya) fills all, O sister.
As the track of a bird in the sky cannot be traced,
as the path of a fish in water cannot be seen,
as a pot in the sky, filled with the water of a mirage, (cannot be grasped),
(such is) Bithal, the Master of Nama, who has burned away the three (fevers). ॥3॥
525.3: Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, Pade of Sri Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The calf has already made the milk its leavings, at the very udder;
the flower the bumblebee has spoiled, and the water the fish.
O mother, what shall I bring to offer in the worship of Gobind?
I find no other flower, none beyond compare.
The sandal trees of Malaya have snakes coiled round them;
poison and Amrit live side by side.
Incense, lamps, food offerings: their fragrance (has already been taken);
how, then, are your servants to worship you?
I offer up my body and mind; this is the worship I lay before (you);
by the Guru's grace I attain the Pure One.
Worship and adoration (with such offerings) are not mine to give you;
says Ravidas: what, then, will my state be? ॥5॥
525.4: Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Pade of Sri Trilochan Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(If) the inner self, filthy (as it is), has not been made pure, (and) outwardly (one wears) the garb of a renunciate,
(if) the lotus of the heart and Brahm within the body have not been recognised, why become a sannyasi?
(The world) has strayed in doubt, O Jai Chand;
it has not, not at all, recognised the Lord of supreme bliss.
(One) ate from house to house and fattened the body, (put on) the patched coat and the earrings, (all) for Maya;
(one) smeared on the ashes of the cremation ground, (but) without the Guru the essence was not found.
Why do you chant, why do you practise austerities, why do you churn water?
Remember the One beyond desire, who created the eighty-four lakh (forms of life).
Why (carry) the water-pot, O wearer of the patched robe? Why wander to the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage)?
Says Trilochan: listen, O mortal: where there is no grain, why spread (the sheaves) for threshing? ॥4॥
526.1: Raag Gujri, the hymn of Bhagat Trilochan Ji.
One who at the very end thinks of wealth, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a snake.
O sister, may the Name of Gobind not be forgotten.
One who at the very end thinks of (his) wife, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a prostitute.
One who at the very end thinks of (his) sons, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a pig.
One who at the very end thinks of mansions, and dies in such thoughts,
is born again and again as a ghost.
One who at the very end thinks of Narayan, and dies in such thoughts,
says Tilochan: that man is liberated; Pitambar, the Lord, dwells in his heart. ॥5॥
526.2: Raag Gujri, Ghar 4, a Pada of Sri Jaidev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(He is) the Supreme, the Origin (of all), the all-pervading Being, beyond compare, endowed with truth and every such quality;
supremely wondrous, beyond Prakriti (the stuff of the world), beyond the reach of thought, reaching everywhere.
Only the Name of Ram, which delights the mind,
utter: it is Amrit, the very essence;
by remembering it, the fear of birth, of old age, of (the mind's) ills and of death no longer torments (one).
If you wish to overcome Jam and his kind, (then) praise (the Lord): that is well-being, that is the good deed to do.
In the present, the past and the future he is wholly imperishable; he is supreme, and ever in bliss.
Greed and the rest, the eye cast on another's home, conduct that goes against what is right,
give up all evil deeds and evil thinking, and run to the refuge of Chakradhar, the Holder of the discus.
The Lord's own devotees are wholly pure, in heart, in deed and in word;
what (is gained) by yoga, what by sacrifices, what by charity, what by austerities?
Repeat Gobind, Gobind, O man: (he is) the abode of all spiritual powers.
Jaidev has come openly to his (refuge), who in the present and the past reaches everywhere. ॥5॥
